description.en: Principles for designing digital tools and services in the UK National Health Service.

principles.title: Put people at the heart of everything you do
principles.description:
Patients, family, carers, staff. Design things that understand and respect people's needs. Take the time to learn about the whole person — their emotional, physical and technical needs.

Design with compassion.

principles.title: Design for the outcome
principles.description:
What will good look like? What are the health, wellbeing or other measurable outcomes that your work will impact?

Your work should improve lives, either directly or indirectly.

principles.title: Be inclusive
principles.description:
NHS services are for everyone.

Make sure people with different physical, mental health, social, cultural or learning needs can use your design.

principles.title: Design for context
principles.description:
Don't just design your part of a service. Consider people's entire experience, and the infrastructure and processes involved.

Think about how people begin and end their time with what you are designing.

principles.title: Design for trust
principles.description:
People trust the NHS. Take care not to jeopardise that.

Design things that are reliable and secure.

principles.title: Test your assumptions
principles.description:
Design and test your work with real people. Observe behaviour and gather evidence. Work with subject experts and existing research.

Do not rely on hunches.

principles.title: Make, learn, iterate
principles.description: Start small. Experiment with different ways of doing things. Make prototypes to improve your understanding. Test and refine.

principles.title: Do the hard work to make it simple
principles.description:
Healthcare journeys can be complex. Take the time to understand what you are trying to solve.

Do not push complexity onto the people using what you are designing.

principles.title: Make things open: it makes things better
principles.description:
Share your learning. Share your work. Be transparent in your design decisions.

Be accountable and have confidence in your solutions.

principles.title: Design to protect the environment
principles.description:
The climate crisis is a health crisis.

Learn about the impact of your design decisions on the environment. Encourage your team to challenge existing processes and re-use resources.

description.en: Foundational principles for digital public services.

principles.title: Start with user needs
principles.description:
Service design starts with identifying user needs. Do research, analyse data, talk to users. Don't make assumptions.

Have empathy for users, and remember that what they ask for isn't always what they need.

principles.title: Do less
principles.description:
Government should only do what only government can do. If we've found a way of doing something that works, we should make it reusable and shareable.

We should concentrate on the irreducible core.

principles.title: Design with data
principles.description:
In most cases, we can learn from real world behaviour by looking at how existing services are used. Let data drive decision-making, not hunches.

Analytics should be built-in, always on and easy to read.

principles.title: Do the hard work to make it simple
principles.description:
Making something look simple is easy. Making something simple to use is much harder.

Don't take "It's always been that way" for an answer. It's usually more and harder work to make things simple, but it's the right thing to do.

principles.title: Iterate. Then iterate again
principles.description:
The best way to build good services is to start small and iterate wildly. Release MVPs early, test with users, refine based on feedback.

Iteration reduces risk. It makes big failures unlikely and turns small failures into lessons.

principles.title: This is for everyone
principles.description:
Accessible design is good design. Everything we build should be as inclusive, legible and readable as possible.

The people who most need our services are often the people who find them hardest to use. Let's think about those people from the start.

principles.title: Understand context
principles.description:
We're not designing for a screen, we're designing for people. We need to think hard about the context in which they're using our services.

Are they in a library? Are they on a phone? Have they never used the web before?

principles.title: Build digital services, not websites
principles.description:
A service is something that helps people to do something. Our job is to uncover user needs, and build the service that meets those needs.

The digital world has to connect to the real world.

principles.title: Be consistent, not uniform
principles.description:
We should use the same language and design patterns wherever possible. This helps people get familiar with our services.

This isn't a straitjacket. When we find patterns that work we should share them — but that shouldn't stop us from improving them.

principles.title: Make things open: it makes things better
principles.description:
We should share what we're doing. Share code, share designs, share ideas, share intentions, share failures.

The more eyes there are on a service the better it gets.

description.en: Product principles for internal platforms at a fintech.
description.pl: Zasady produktowe Monzo dla wewnętrznych platform.

principles.title: Care about our platform contributors
principles.description: Build extensible platforms that are inclusive and accessible to many contributors, focusing on technical solutions while maintaining strong developer experience.

principles.title: Optimise for learning with simple solutions
principles.description: Focus on building the simplest thing to generate data and knowledge for better decisions. Use MVPs to learn before investing in automation.

principles.title: Prove it
principles.description: Test and measure everything built with quantitative or qualitative data. Build in data gathering capabilities from the start.

principles.title: Teach, guide, and empower
principles.description: Design solutions that reduce mistakes and increase confidence. Embed training and customize user experience automatically while allowing personalization.

principles.title: Let consistency and patterns build trust
principles.description: Build predictable products with high conceptual integrity that let users develop reliable mental models for intuitive navigation and confident action.

principles.title: Keep the big picture in mind
principles.description: Focus on outcomes and workflows rather than feature aggregation. Ensure holistic and consistent experiences.

description.en: Apple's iOS design principles.

principles.title: Aesthetic Integrity
principles.description: Aesthetic integrity represents how well an app's appearance and behavior integrate with its function. Serious apps maintain focus through subtle design, while immersive apps deliver captivating experiences that encourage discovery.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: A consistent app implements familiar standards and paradigms by using system-provided interface elements, well-known icons, standard text styles, and uniform terminology.

principles.title: Direct Manipulation
principles.description: The direct manipulation of onscreen content engages people and facilitates understanding. Users see immediate visible results when rotating devices or using gestures.

principles.title: Feedback
principles.description: Feedback acknowledges actions and shows results to keep people informed. iOS apps provide perceptible responses through element highlighting, progress indicators, animation, and sound.

principles.title: Metaphors
principles.description: People learn more quickly when an app's virtual objects and actions are metaphors for familiar experiences. Physical interaction with screens — dragging, swiping, toggling — leverages real-world understanding.

principles.title: User Control
principles.description: Throughout iOS, people — not apps — are in control. Apps should suggest actions and warn of consequences while keeping interactive elements familiar.

description.en: Google's Material Design system.

principles.title: Material is the metaphor
principles.description: A material metaphor is the unifying theory of a rationalized space and a system of motion. Physical surfaces provide visual cues grounded in reality, helping users understand affordances through familiar tactile attributes.

principles.title: Bold, graphic, intentional
principles.description: Print design fundamentals — typography, grids, space, scale, color, and imagery — guide visual treatments that establish hierarchy, meaning, and focus. Deliberate color choices, edge-to-edge imagery, large-scale typography, and intentional white space create a bold and graphic interface.

principles.title: Motion provides meaning
principles.description: Motion respects and reinforces the user as the prime mover. Motion is meaningful and appropriate, serving to focus attention and maintain continuity through subtle yet clear feedback and efficient, coherent transitions.

description.en: IBM's principles for complex enterprise software.
description.pl: Zasady IBM dla złożonego oprogramowania enterprise.

principles.title: Domain Expertise Should Be Central
principles.description: Concepts from the product's subject domain should be central and apparent in the software design, so users can leverage existing knowledge when learning new software.

principles.title: Keep It Simple
principles.description: Give easy access to the features that most users will need most of the time; features used less often or by only a subset of users are placed less prominently.

principles.title: Optimize for Frequent Tasks
principles.description: Understanding how users will use the software you are designing is critically important to anticipate required information, task flows, and features at key interaction points.

principles.title: Make Interface Accessible and Visible
principles.description: Design so users can view and easily access objects or information within the interface rather than hiding choices behind cryptic sequences.

principles.title: Use Proper Default Values
principles.description: Employ sensible defaults to help users complete tasks relatively easily and quickly rather than overwhelming them with choices.

principles.title: Be Flexible
principles.description: Allow customization for unique needs and don't limit users by artificially restricting their choices to a correct sequence.

principles.title: Keep Users Informed and in Control
principles.description: Provide informative and timely feedback tailored to the current situation, including progress indicators and alerts about data loss.

principles.title: Consistency in Appearance and Behavior
principles.description: Things that look the same should behave in the same way, and an action should always produce the same result.

principles.title: Enable Undo and Redo
principles.description: Applications must provide users with the ability to freely explore applications without fearing permanent damage.

principles.title: Use Industry Standard Conventions
principles.description: Apply standard selection models and keyboard equivalents like Ctrl+C consistently across contexts.

principles.title: Keep Target Users in Mind
principles.description: Develop personas and understand typical workflows to create designs that resonate with actual user needs.

principles.title: Avoid Feature Bloat
principles.description: Every additional feature equals a set of choices added to what is likely already a wide array of choices.

principles.title: Design for Localization
principles.description: Create interfaces accommodating longer German translations without requiring redesign for different geographies.

principles.title: Consider Accessibility
principles.description: Design for persons with disabilities including those with impaired vision or physical limitations.

principles.title: Provide Contextual Help
principles.description: Make help available to users when they need it so they don't constantly consult documentation.

principles.title: Use Good Visual Design
principles.description: Visual design should surface to the user in a cohesive manner all aspects of the design principles as an integral part of the process.

principles.title: Promote Clarity and Visual Simplicity
principles.description: Apply subtractive design, visual hierarchy, affordance, and visual schemes to reduce clutter and support the user model.

description.en: Figma's principles for design tools.

principles.title: Powerful
principles.description: Design is about finding novel solutions for complex problems. Figma must enable users to explore and express any idea through robust capabilities.

principles.title: Precise
principles.description: Figma is a tool for experts and professionals for which accuracy is critical. The platform allows users to maintain exactness across all functions.

principles.title: Systematic
principles.description: Leveraging reusable components enables creation of increasingly sophisticated designs while computers handle repetitive tasks.

principles.title: Predictable
principles.description: When features are added we strive to respect the system, building on users trust and prior experience. New patterns are introduced thoughtfully.

principles.title: Biased toward simplicity
principles.description: Keep the simple things simple, and make the complex things possible. Active effort counters the natural drift toward unnecessary complexity.

principles.title: Natural mental models
principles.description: Solutions align with how humans think rather than computer operations, supporting intuitive tool comprehension.

principles.title: Responsible
principles.description: The company challenges conventions while learning from others, avoiding repetitive approaches.

principles.title: Detail-oriented
principles.description: We bring delight with details. Precision in craft inspires users to maintain equally high standards.

principles.title: Respectful
principles.description: User attention is valued and protected through research-based understanding rather than assumptions.

description.en: Atlassian's design principles.

principles.title: Build trust in every interaction
principles.description: Trust is earned throughout the Atlassian experience across all interactions. The principle emphasizes meeting expectations around functionality, reliability, error prevention, recovery, speed, and security.

principles.title: Connect people to collaborate better
principles.description: Products should bring people together as teams rather than individuals. They prioritize accessibility, inclusivity, and openness.

principles.title: Match purpose and feel familiar
principles.description: Products maintain visual and behavioral consistency while adapting to different devices and contexts.

principles.title: Drive momentum from end to end
principles.description: Design should respect the work people need to accomplish, knowing when to assist and when to step back.

principles.title: Guide mastery for greater value
principles.description: Products should be satisfying to master from initial evaluation through advanced configuration. They reveal capabilities progressively over time.

description.en: Spotify's principles for music streaming.

principles.title: Relevant
principles.description: Present the right information at the right time by being thoughtful about what is shown, to whom, and in what context.

principles.title: Human
principles.description: Balance emotion and logic to create intuitive, conversational experiences that feel dynamic like culture itself.

principles.title: Unified
principles.description: Maintain coherence across products by following the design system, reusing and adapting existing patterns rather than reinventing.

description.en: Shopify's Polaris design system.

principles.title: Put merchants first
principles.description: Think about the needs of different types of merchants. Use research to inform decisions and map your process to how real merchants think and work.

principles.title: Empower but don't overwhelm
principles.description: Build powerful tools that feel effortless. Remove unnecessary steps and make sure people understand what they need to do throughout.

principles.title: Build a cohesive experience
principles.description: Use consistent language, patterns, and components across the interface so merchants can get things done without relearning how things work.

principles.title: Be polished but not ornamental
principles.description: Look good and feel world-class, but not for the sake of being pretty. Every aesthetic decision should be purposeful.

description.en: Fluent — Microsoft's unified design language across Windows, Office, Xbox.

principles.title: Natural on every platform
principles.description: Experiences should adapt to the device you're on and build off the familiar, designing for what you already understand while reusing native platform components and patterns.

principles.title: Built for focus
principles.description: Experiences should inspire action and draw you forward simply and seamlessly, with less visual clutter and noise to keep people centered, calm, and confident.

principles.title: One for all, all for one
principles.description: Experiences should consider, learn, and reflect a range of perspectives and abilities for the benefit of all, including diverse people earlier in the design process.

principles.title: Unmistakably Microsoft
principles.description: Experiences should feel like one Microsoft across products, focusing energy on signature experiences that connect products together with distinctively Microsoft branding.

description.en: Slack's product principles for team communication.

principles.title: Don't make me think
principles.description: Ensure using Slack feels effortless by reducing cognitive load at every step, giving users more time to focus on work that matters most.

principles.title: Be a great host
principles.description: Make users feel comfortable and happy by viewing Slack as their host, creating a welcoming environment that feels human and approachable.

principles.title: Prototype the path
principles.description: Collaborate with customers using Slack Connect to develop products and features, learning from how customers actually use features rather than debating aspirational ideas.

principles.title: Don't reinvent the wheel
principles.description: Learn from existing patterns and solutions rather than creating everything from scratch, building on proven approaches to deliver better experiences faster.

principles.title: Make bigger, bolder bets
principles.description: Focus on incremental moves that improve customers' working lives by climbing smaller hills to gain new perspectives rather than attempting distant, risky leaps.

description.en: Airbnb's design principles for hospitality.

principles.title: Unified
principles.description: Each piece is part of a greater whole and should contribute positively to the system at scale. There should be no isolated features or outliers.

principles.title: Universal
principles.description: Airbnb is used around the world by a wide global community. Our products and visual language should be welcoming and accessible.

principles.title: Iconic
principles.description: We're focused when it comes to both design and functionality. Our work should speak boldly and clearly to this focus.

principles.title: Conversational
principles.description: Our use of motion breathes life into our products, and allows us to communicate with users in easily understood ways.

description.en: Adobe Spectrum design system principles.

principles.title: Rational
principles.description: Spectrum is based on real-world situations. Every component, pattern, and principle is informed by research and thoughtful testing.

principles.title: Human
principles.description: Spectrum places customer needs first. It's deeply committed to a high standard of accessibility, honesty, and respect for user attention.

principles.title: Focused
principles.description: Spectrum strives to deliver what's needed, when it's needed. No unnecessary decoration or irrelevant content.

description.en: Pinterest's design principles for visual exploration.

principles.title: Lucid
principles.description: It's intuitive, not learned. It makes the user feel powerful. It makes the content taste better.

principles.title: Animated
principles.description: It's colorful. It's visually responsive. It's unexpected.

principles.title: Unbreakable
principles.description: It's built for exploration. It's impossible to mis-tap. It's reversible.

description.en: Open-source inclusive design principles (Microsoft, Heydon Pickering et al).

principles.title: Provide Comparable Experience
principles.description: Ensure your interface provides a comparable experience for all so people can accomplish tasks in a way that suits their needs without undermining the quality of the content.

principles.title: Consider Situation
principles.description: People use your interface in different situations. Make sure your interface delivers a valuable experience to people regardless of their circumstances.

principles.title: Be Consistent
principles.description: Use familiar conventions and apply them consistently.

principles.title: Give Control
principles.description: Ensure people are in control. People should be able to access and interact with content in their preferred way.

principles.title: Offer Choice
principles.description: Consider providing different ways for people to complete tasks, especially those that are complex or non standard.

principles.title: Prioritise Content
principles.description: Help users focus on core tasks, features, and information by prioritising them within the content and layout.

principles.title: Add Value
principles.description: Consider the value of features and how they improve the experience for different users.

description.en: Google's principles for responsible AI development.

principles.title: Bold innovation
principles.description: Develop AI that assists, empowers, and inspires people across fields, driving economic progress and improving lives while advancing research and solving real-world problems with measurable outcomes.

principles.title: Responsible development and deployment
principles.description: Pursue AI responsibly throughout the development lifecycle with appropriate human oversight, safety research, rigorous testing, and safeguards to mitigate unintended outcomes and protect privacy.

principles.title: Collaborative progress, together
principles.description: Develop AI as a foundational technology that enables others to innovate, collaborating with researchers, governments, and civil society to foster a vibrant ecosystem of innovative tools.

description.en: BBC's design philosophy across digital products.
description.pl: Filozofia projektowa BBC w produktach cyfrowych.

principles.title: Universal
principles.description: Our messages are clear and are communicated through simple, useful and intuitive interfaces. Our services are inherently open and accessible.

principles.title: Compelling
principles.description: Our voice ranges from serious and authoritative through to witty and entertaining. We sound authentic and relevant, warm and human. We engage our audiences with compelling storytelling.

principles.title: Authentic
principles.description: We value the familiarity and trust placed in us. We acknowledge the BBC's heritage of iconic design and broadcasting history with subtle references.

principles.title: Pioneering
principles.description: We pioneer design innovations that surprise and delight. We introduce the unexpected but always take our audiences with us.

principles.title: Current
principles.description: We curate a timeline of Britain; reflecting the present as it happens and adding relevant contextual links with the past.

principles.title: Distinctive
principles.description: We stand out by looking to tomorrow instead of simply referencing the design trends of today. We strike a balance between cookie-cutter design and beautiful anarchy.

principles.title: Joined-up
principles.description: All our services and platforms are one connected whole which deliver experiences sensitive to their context of use. We enable coherent journeys both within and outside familiar paths.

principles.title: Local/Global
principles.description: We need to speak to everyone but we recognise the individual. Our message is scalable and localisable.

principles.title: Modern British
principles.description: Our services are woven into the fabric of everyday life in the UK. They embrace a modern British design aesthetic that extends outside national boundaries. Our character is vibrant and sometimes quirky.

principles.title: Best
principles.description: Last but not least we put quality first.

description.en: Etsy's design principles for handmade commerce.

principles.title: Be Effective
principles.description: Excellent design means satisfying customer's needs. It's asking, 'are we solving the right problems, in the best way, for the right people?' Learn from feedback, listen to peers and customers.

principles.title: Create Unity
principles.description: Excellent design means unity. It's asking, 'does everything we do feel essential, and work together to create a holistic experience?' Champion design systems, align brand elements.

principles.title: Always Be Thorough
principles.description: Gather feedback, listen to stakeholders, maintain an empathetic perspective, and be receptive to different viewpoints.

principles.title: Express Etsy
principles.description: Excellent design means boldly being ourselves. Are we bravely expressing who we are in what we make? Stand by convictions and values.

description.en: Intercom's product design principles.

principles.title: Connected, modular systems
principles.description: We favor modular systems over bespoke optimizations. We reuse, evolve and merge before creating something new.

principles.title: Opinionated by default, flexible under the hood
principles.description: We optimize our designs to feel simple and opinionated by default, but progressively reveal power and flexibility.

principles.title: Follow the fundamentals
principles.description: We favor established best practices and avoid overly clever, non-standard design patterns.

principles.title: Make it feel personal
principles.description: Our designs reflect that we're connecting real people, not entries in a database.

principles.title: What you ship is what matters
principles.description: Our deliverable is not the design file. We take pride and ownership of what we ship.

description.en: U.S. Government's design system principles.

principles.title: Make the best thing the easiest thing
principles.description: Provide the easiest path for federal teams to comply with policy through open-source, mobile-first code and assets.

principles.title: Offer accessibility out of the box
principles.description: Every asset meets Section 508 accessibility standards, with guidance for compliant customisations.

principles.title: Design for flexibility
principles.description: Patterns adapt to diverse government needs, focusing on performance and user validation.

principles.title: Showcase benefits for agency and users
principles.description: Catalogue successes to inspire teams and support the business case for adoption.

principles.title: Reuse, reuse, reuse
principles.description: Provide tried-and-true components so teams can focus on unique aspects rather than recreating basics.

description.en: Salesforce Lightning Design System principles.

principles.title: Clarity
principles.description: Eliminate ambiguity and enable people to see, understand, and act with confidence.

principles.title: Efficiency
principles.description: Streamline and optimise workflows by intelligently anticipating needs to help people work better, smarter, and faster.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: Create familiarity and strengthen intuition by applying the same solution to the same problem.

principles.title: Beauty
principles.description: Demonstrate respect for people's time and attention through thoughtful and elegant craftsmanship.

description.en: Uber's design principles for ride-hailing.

principles.title: Instructive
principles.description: Guide users clearly through what they need to do. Provide direction without requiring them to figure things out themselves.

principles.title: Non-intrusive
principles.description: Respect the user's primary task — in this case, driving safely. Don't demand attention at dangerous moments.

principles.title: Focused and Timely
principles.description: Show only what's relevant right now. Information should appear when needed and disappear when it's not.

description.en: Lyft's brand and product design principles.

principles.title: Nail the Basics
principles.description: Clear choice and context — establishes foundational clarity and situational awareness for users to make informed decisions.

principles.title: Build Confidence
principles.description: Consistent and transparent — creates trust through predictable interactions and openness about how the product works.

principles.title: Be Unique
principles.description: Ownable and delightful — develops distinctive character while delivering pleasurable experiences that set the brand apart.

description.en: Asana's design principles.

principles.title: Allow users to focus on their work without interference
principles.description: A user's focus should be in their control, only distract users with changes that are personally relevant.

principles.title: Increase confidence through clarity
principles.description: Within the application, and more broadly within teams, it is unambiguous what is happening and why.

principles.title: Foster productive and emotionally satisfying interpersonal dynamics
principles.description: Users feel like they are part of a team, where they can count on each other to do their part, and feel like they're moving forward towards a common goal.

principles.title: Design for fast, effortless, and intentional interactions
principles.description: Simple and common tasks should be frictionless and obvious; complex tasks should feel efficient and delightful. But speed should not lead to inaccuracies.

principles.title: Empower everyone through progressive discoverability
principles.description: Everyone at all levels of experience with Asana should feel like they know how to use the product, regardless of how many features they use.

principles.title: Be consistent and standard, and innovate when it's worth it
principles.description: Users should feel like Asana is familiar, yet modern.

description.en: HubSpot's design principles.

principles.title: Clear
principles.description: We design for clarity and focus. Our work helps users do the next right thing through feature prioritization, visual hierarchy, and contextual awareness.

principles.title: Human
principles.description: We foster a sense of joy by humanizing the experience in ways that resonate across cultures. Our work provides users with a playful and personable interaction every time.

principles.title: Inbound
principles.description: We reinforce the message and meaning of the Inbound methodology. Our work makes the Inbound path clear to our users and helps them understand why it's the right thing to do.

principles.title: Integrated
principles.description: We design for systems that work together seamlessly across the platform.

principles.title: Collaborative
principles.description: We devise powerful systems that encourage people to work seamlessly together. Our work helps people create and collaborate with each other in natural, intuitive ways.

description.en: SAP Fiori design principles for enterprise.

principles.title: Role-based
principles.description: Interfaces are tailored to individual user roles, showing only the functionality relevant to each person's tasks and responsibilities.

principles.title: Delightful
principles.description: User journeys are designed through research and iterative testing to ensure intuitive navigation and minimal learning curves.

principles.title: Coherent
principles.description: Unified design patterns across all applications reduce cognitive load and make learning new tools predictable.

principles.title: Simple
principles.description: Interfaces focus on essential information, eliminating unnecessary interactions and streamlining effort.

principles.title: Adaptive
principles.description: Experiences adapt seamlessly across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices without compromising usability.

description.en: Microsoft's Responsible AI principles.

principles.title: Fairness
principles.description: AI systems should treat all people fairly when allocating opportunities, resources, and information, ensuring equitable treatment across different user groups and contexts.

principles.title: Reliability and Safety
principles.description: AI systems should perform reliably and safely across different use conditions and contexts, including ones they weren't originally intended for, maintaining consistent performance.

principles.title: Privacy and Security
principles.description: AI systems should be secure and respect privacy by design, protecting user data and ensuring systems are built with privacy and security considerations from the start.

principles.title: Inclusiveness
principles.description: AI systems should empower everyone and engage all people regardless of their backgrounds or abilities, ensuring accessibility and usability for diverse user populations.

principles.title: Transparency
principles.description: AI systems should be understandable so people correctly comprehend their capabilities, limitations, and decision-making processes for informed interaction.

principles.title: Accountability
principles.description: People should be accountable for AI systems through proper oversight and control mechanisms, ensuring humans remain in control and can address system impacts.

description.en: Don Norman's foundational principles from "The Design of Everyday Things".
description.pl: Fundamentalne zasady Dona Normana z "The Design of Everyday Things".

principles.title: Visibility
principles.description: Make possible actions visible so users don't have to guess what to do next. When key actions are hidden, users rely on memory or trial and error.

principles.title: Feedback
principles.description: Show the result of an action immediately so users know what just happened. Without feedback, users repeat actions or assume nothing worked.

principles.title: Constraints
principles.description: Limit what users can do at a given moment to prevent errors. Good constraints remove invalid options rather than warning after the fact.

principles.title: Mapping
principles.description: Align controls with their effects so the outcome feels predictable. When mapping is unclear, users must learn arbitrary relationships instead of relying on intuition.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: Use the same patterns for similar actions so users don't have to relearn behaviour. Inconsistency forces users to stop and think.

principles.title: Affordance
principles.description: Design elements so their use is obvious from their appearance. When affordances are unclear, users rely on labels or guesswork.

description.en: John Maeda's Laws of Simplicity — a foundational framework for simplicity in design.
description.pl: Prawa prostoty Johna Maedy — fundamentalny framework dla prostoty w designie.

principles.title: Reduce
principles.description: The simplest way to achieve simplicity is through thoughtful reduction.

principles.title: Organize
principles.description: Organization makes a system of many appear fewer.

principles.title: Time
principles.description: Savings in time feel like simplicity.

principles.title: Learn
principles.description: Knowledge makes everything simpler.

principles.title: Differences
principles.description: Simplicity and complexity need each other.

principles.title: Context
principles.description: What lies in the periphery of simplicity is definitely not peripheral.

principles.title: Emotion
principles.description: More emotions are better than less.

principles.title: Trust
principles.description: In simplicity we trust.

principles.title: Failure
principles.description: Some things can never be made simple.

principles.title: The One
principles.description: Simplicity is about subtracting the obvious, and adding the meaningful.

description.en: The UNIX philosophy by Ken Thompson, Dennis Ritchie, et al.

principles.title: Do One Thing and Do It Well
principles.description: Make each program do one thing well. To do a new job, build afresh rather than complicate old programs by adding new features. Focus on singular purpose rather than feature bloat.

principles.title: Write Programs to Work Together
principles.description: Expect the output of every program to become the input to another, as yet unknown, program. Design outputs as clean inputs for other tools.

principles.title: Build a Prototype as Soon as Possible
principles.description: Design and build software, even operating systems, to be tried early, ideally within weeks. Prioritize rapid iteration and refinement over perfection.

principles.title: Build Software Tools
principles.description: Use tools in preference to unskilled help to lighten a programming task, even if you have to detour to build the tools.

description.en: Ant Design — design system from Alibaba's Ant Financial.

principles.title: Proximity
principles.description: When several items are in close proximity to each other, they become one visual unit rather than separate ones. Distance should be larger to distinguish units.

principles.title: Alignment
principles.description: Following Gestalt psychology's Law of Continuity, aligning interface elements matches user perception and delivers information smoothly.

principles.title: Contrast
principles.description: An effective method to add visual interest and establish organizational hierarchy among elements, helping users locate information more quickly.

principles.title: Repetition
principles.description: Consistent use of identical elements throughout reduces learning costs and helps users recognize connections between related components.

principles.title: Make it Direct
principles.description: Where there is output, let there be input — enable direct manipulation by allowing users to edit content in context rather than on separate pages.

principles.title: Stay on the Page
principles.description: Resolve most issues without navigation away, preventing change blindness and mental disruption caused by page refreshes or forwarding.

principles.title: Keep it Lightweight
principles.description: Apply Fitts's Law by positioning tools contextually and making them large enough to target, improving user interaction through lightweight, accessible placement.

principles.title: Provide an Invitation
principles.description: Offer visual cues and just-in-time tips that guide users through interactions and hint at what happens next.

principles.title: Use Transition
principles.description: Employ movement, shape changes, and color transitions to smooth visual changes and make them appear natural.

principles.title: React Immediately
principles.description: Provide instant feedback after each user action — buttons depress, text appears, errors display — so the system feels responsive rather than sluggish.

description.en: Firefox Photon design principles from Mozilla.

principles.title: Adaptable
principles.description: Work across different platforms, screen sizes, and contexts. Respect each environment's conventions while maintaining Firefox's identity.

principles.title: Quick
principles.description: Feel fast and responsive. Minimise perceived wait times and ensure interactions feel immediate and fluid.

principles.title: Aware
principles.description: Understand context and anticipate needs. Provide relevant information and options based on what the user is doing.

principles.title: Approachable
principles.description: Feel welcoming and easy to use for everyone. Avoid jargon and make features discoverable without overwhelming new users.

principles.title: Supportive
principles.description: Help users accomplish their goals. Provide guidance when needed and recover gracefully from errors.

principles.title: Whimsical
principles.description: Include moments of delight and personality. A browser can be serious about privacy while still feeling human and warm.

description.en: Quartz's design principles for digital journalism.
description.pl: Zasady projektowe Quartz dla cyfrowego dziennikarstwa.

principles.title: Stay out of the users' way
principles.description: Don't interrupt the reading experience. The interface should be invisible, letting readers focus on content.

principles.title: Let the stories shine
principles.description: Design should serve journalism, not compete with it. The content is the product.

principles.title: Make sure it works on mobile
principles.description: Mobile isn't an afterthought — it's where most readers are. Design for small screens first.

principles.title: Remove before adding
principles.description: Question every element. If something can be removed without harm, remove it.

principles.title: Pick one thing before another
principles.description: Prioritise ruthlessly. Not everything can be equally important on the page.

principles.title: Make small decisions on data and big decisions with your gut
principles.description: Use analytics for incremental improvements, but trust editorial judgement for strategic choices.

description.en: Financial Times product principles for financial journalism.

principles.title: Be Distinct
principles.description: Build bold products that stand out from competition. Make the most of FT's reputation for innovation, insight and integrity, ensuring products jump out like the FT does on newsstands.

principles.title: Become Indispensable
principles.description: Focus on what users need and make that the core of what you build. Create products that are essential to users' success and a joy to use.

principles.title: Provably Brilliant
principles.description: Go beyond good ideas by measuring what changes will have the biggest impact. Use data from experiments and tweaks to learn and improve.

principles.title: Products Are Partnerships
principles.description: Embrace diverse expertise from around the company and collaborate within teams. Empower others to succeed.

principles.title: Build on Every Success (and Failure)
principles.description: Investigate, iterate, and repeat as needs and expectations change. Strive for simplicity and prune or retire features when they've served their purpose.

description.en: Tailwind CSS design principles.

principles.title: Everyone Drives Design
principles.description: Anyone who impacts the product is part of the design process. Collectively, a diverse team designs better products.

principles.title: Balance Obvious, Easy, and Possible
principles.description: Make intimidating tasks feel delightfully easy. Simplify complex systems and workflows so users can take action and make choices.

principles.title: What's Vital for Some is Valuable for Everyone
principles.description: Champion inclusive and accessible solutions. Design that's vital for a minority brings value to the majority — accessible design equals usable design.

principles.title: Data Driven Design Over Assumptions
principles.description: Rely on qualitative and quantitative data to guide difficult decisions. Ship high-impact features based on validated needs.

description.en: GitLab's Pajamas Design System principles.

principles.title: Sophisticated simplicity
principles.description: Make thoughtful choices that streamline complex workflows and functionality, helping users stay focused on what matters most without unnecessary gimmicks.

principles.title: Design for natural developer flow
principles.description: Enable users to move seamlessly through tasks without context switching, prioritising workflow continuity over feature isolation.

principles.title: Start simple, reveal complexity gradually
principles.description: Show only what users need now with advanced features discoverable when needed, providing zero-configuration setup for common use cases.

principles.title: Make everything feel like one product
principles.description: Use consistent patterns so learning transfers across all features with unified design system, terminology, and predictable interactions.

principles.title: Make every interaction feel instant
principles.description: Design for speed from the start with sub-second response for common actions and progressive loading for complex operations.

principles.title: Show what's happening and why
principles.description: Users should always understand system status and how to fix problems with clear indicators, comprehensive logs, and intuitive debugging.

principles.title: Build for teams, not just individuals
principles.description: Make sharing, discussing, and collaborating effortless, facilitating teamwork and communication across all features.

principles.title: Always provide a clear next step
principles.description: Never show problems without solutions or data without actions, providing smart recommendations and clear next steps for every state.

principles.title: Enable customization within guardrails
principles.description: Let teams work their way while maintaining platform coherence through flexible configuration with smart defaults and inheritance patterns.

principles.title: Design for scale and compliance always
principles.description: Build in governance, security, and audit capabilities from the start with role-based access control and complete audit trails.

principles.title: Make it a joy to use
principles.description: Craft delightful experiences that developers will champion with keyboard shortcuts, accessibility features, and thoughtful micro-interactions.

description.en: PayPal's design principles.

principles.title: We Craft
principles.description: Obsess over every pixel and word. Focus on details to build something truly memorable and release only work we're proud of.

principles.title: We Simplify
principles.description: Respect users' time by making things simpler. Simple is loved, needed, used, and shared — be honest about our impact on people's lives.

principles.title: We Connect
principles.description: Create opportunity by connecting people to each other. Find ways to further interconnect our world and dive into this challenge headfirst.

principles.title: We Go All In
principles.description: Invent then reinvent, design then redesign. Fight for customers by doing our best work so they can do their best work.

description.en: Twilio Paste Design System principles.

principles.title: It's Inclusive
principles.description: Build a floor for every experience. Consider voices of people who don't look like us, speak different languages, or use our work in different ways.

principles.title: It's a Multiplier
principles.description: Only work on something if it's a base common denominator for exceptional experiences. Work should multiply upstream and downstream efforts.

principles.title: It's Referenceable
principles.description: Systems should never have single points of failure. Good documentation, reliable APIs, and intuitive language ensure what we do works well.

description.en: Google's foundational "Ten Things We Know to Be True".

principles.title: Focus on the user and all else will follow
principles.description: We take great care to ensure that they will ultimately serve you, rather than our own internal goal or bottom line. Google prioritizes user experience over profits.

principles.title: It's best to do one thing really, really well
principles.description: The company concentrates on search excellence, using one of the world's largest research groups focused exclusively on solving search problems.

principles.title: Fast is better than slow
principles.description: Your time is valuable, so when you're seeking an answer on the web you want it right away. Google optimizes page speed and server efficiency.

principles.title: Democracy on the web works
principles.description: Google's PageRank algorithm evaluates pages based on millions of individuals posting links on websites, treating each new site as another vote.

principles.title: You don't need to be at your desk to need an answer
principles.description: Recognizing the world is increasingly mobile, Google develops mobile technologies and created Android — a free, open source mobile platform.

principles.title: You can make money without doing evil
principles.description: Google generates revenue through relevant advertising while maintaining principles: ads should be relevant and clearly identified.

principles.title: There's always more information out there
principles.description: Beyond HTML pages, Google indexed phone number lookups, news archives, patents, academic journals, billions of images and millions of books.

principles.title: The need for information crosses all borders
principles.description: Operating in more than 60 countries with more than 180 Internet domains, Google offers search interface in more than 130 languages.

principles.title: You can be serious without a suit
principles.description: Google fosters creativity through casual culture where new ideas emerge in a café line and are traded, tested and put into practice with dizzying speed.

principles.title: Great just isn't good enough
principles.description: We set ourselves goals we know we can't reach yet, because we know that by stretching to meet them we can get further than we expected.

description.en: Seven beliefs guiding Facebook's design — universal, human, transparent.
description.pl: Siedem przekonań kierujących designem Facebooka — uniwersalność, ludzkość, przejrzystość.

principles.title: Universal
principles.description: Our mission is to make the entire world more open, and this means reaching every corner, every person. So our design needs to work for everyone, every culture, every language, every device, every stage of life.

principles.title: Human
principles.description: Users return to our site to be surrounded by friends and other people near to them. This is a central promise of our product, that the people you care about are all in one place.

principles.title: Clean
principles.description: Our visual style is clean and understated, to create a blank canvas on which our users live. A minimal, well-lit space encourages participation and honest transparent communication.

principles.title: Consistent
principles.description: We invest our time wisely, by embracing patterns, recognizing that our usability is greatly improved when similar parts are expressed in similar ways.

principles.title: Useful
principles.description: Our product is more utility than entertainment, meant for repeated daily use, providing value efficiently.

principles.title: Fast
principles.description: We value our users time more than our own. We recognize faster experiences are more efficient and feel more effortless.

principles.title: Transparent
principles.description: Users trust us with their identity, their photos, their thoughts and conversation. We reciprocate with the utmost honesty and transparency.

description.en: Five principles for familiar yet original e-commerce.
description.pl: Pięć zasad dla znanego, lecz oryginalnego e-commerce.

principles.title: Original but familiar
principles.description: Our experiences are original but familiar. We strive for intuitive and consistent experiences and differentiate only in places where it really matters.

principles.title: Complexity removed
principles.description: Our products remove the complexity of a dual-sided marketplace by simplifying interactions and guiding our users.

principles.title: Smart and personalized
principles.description: Our products are smart and personalized. We learn from our users about who they are and what they like, delivering a tailored experience.

principles.title: Beautiful expression
principles.description: Our aesthetic is a beautiful expression of our brand traits - real, spirited, smart and dependable.

principles.title: One experience
principles.description: Our product is one coherent experience end to end, even though it is made up of many distinct pieces across various touchpoints and devices.

description.en: Early design principles framed as positive oppositions.
description.pl: Wczesne zasady designu Medium w formie pozytywnych opozycji.

principles.title: Direction over Choice
principles.description: We purposely traded layout, type, and color choices for guidance and direction. Direction was more appropriate for the product because we wanted people to focus on writing, and not get distracted by choice.

principles.title: Appropriate over Consistent
principles.description: We were willing to break consistency if it was more appropriate for the OS, device, or context.

principles.title: Evolving over Finalized
principles.description: The content on Medium should be antifragile, improving with use and evolving overtime. We did not want to design printed books for the internet.

description.en: Ten principles for visual, tactile project management.
description.pl: Dziesięć zasad wizualnego, namacalnego zarządzania projektami.

principles.title: Universal
principles.description: Work for everyone regardless of their role, industry, or technical ability. The tool should adapt to how people naturally think about work.

principles.title: Easy
principles.description: Keep the learning curve shallow. Users should understand how to use the product within moments of seeing it.

principles.title: Personal
principles.description: Let users make the tool their own. Support different working styles and preferences without forcing a single approach.

principles.title: Visual and Tactile
principles.description: Make information visible and interactions feel physical. Moving cards should feel like moving real objects.

principles.title: Familiar
principles.description: Draw on patterns people already know. Use metaphors from the physical world that translate naturally to digital.

principles.title: Succinct
principles.description: Say only what needs to be said. Remove unnecessary words, options, and visual noise.

principles.title: Direct
principles.description: Let users interact with content directly rather than through menus and dialogs. Reduce the steps between intention and action.

principles.title: Flexible
principles.description: Support many different workflows without prescribing how people should work. Adapt to users, not the other way around.

principles.title: Collaborative
principles.description: Make working together feel natural. Keep everyone informed without overwhelming them with notifications.

principles.title: Fun
principles.description: Inject moments of delight. Work is serious, but the tools we use don't have to feel heavy.

description.en: Seven principles for automotive design as brand expression.
description.pl: Siedem zasad designu motoryzacyjnego jako wyraz marki.

principles.title: Design as a trademark
principles.description: For Mercedes-Benz, design is literally a trademark. Because for over 100 years, design has characterized the image of the brand with the three-pointed star and has made visible typical Mercedes brand values such as fascination, responsibility and perfection.

principles.title: Identity and continuity
principles.description: However, in order to build up and care adequately for such a successful brand image, long-term strategies and conceptual continuity are essential. New Mercedes models must indeed formally create a bridge to the future, but at the same time their lines may not abandon their origin.

principles.title: Trends and reality
principles.description: Recognizing and shaping trends are important tasks of the auto designers. They live in the present, but their realm of action is the future.

principles.title: Passion and practicality
principles.description: It is all about people, or, more specifically, about customers and their personality. Because driving a car today means a lot more than reaching your destination in safety and comfort.

principles.title: Experience and enjoyment
principles.description: The interior of a car is conceived as a space for living, one where a lot of time is spent. That is why a pleasant environment is playing an increasingly important role in the motor car, too.

principles.title: Form and function
principles.description: Function and aesthetics, technology and art: what at first sight sounds contradictory has to blend into a harmonious overall concept in a modern car. The objective has been attained if design work and the engineering arts complement each other on a sophisticated level.

principles.title: Visions and emotions
principles.description: A motor vehicle is always perceived with one's senses. No-one can evade its emotional effect. Long before one has any idea about the relevant technical facts or innovations, through its mere appearance – that is, through its design – it awakens desires.

description.en: Ten foundational principles of good design.

principles.title: Good design is innovative
principles.description: The possibilities for innovation are not, by any means, exhausted.

principles.title: Good design makes a product useful
principles.description: A product is bought to be used. It has to satisfy certain criteria, not only functional, but also psychological and aesthetic.

principles.title: Good design is aesthetic
principles.description: The aesthetic quality of a product is integral to its usefulness because products we use every day affect our person and our well-being.

principles.title: Good design makes a product understandable
principles.description: It clarifies the product's structure. Better still, it can make the product talk. At best, it is self-explanatory.

principles.title: Good design is unobtrusive
principles.description: Their design should therefore be both neutral and restrained, to leave room for the user's self-expression.

principles.title: Good design is honest
principles.description: It does not make a product more innovative, powerful or valuable than it really is.

principles.title: Good design is long-lasting
principles.description: Unlike fashionable design, it lasts many years – even in today's throwaway society.

principles.title: Good design is thorough down to the last detail
principles.description: Nothing must be arbitrary or left to chance.

principles.title: Good design is environmentally friendly
principles.description: Design makes an important contribution to the preservation of the environment.

principles.title: Good design is as little design as possible
principles.description: Less, but better – because it concentrates on the essential aspects.

description.en: Six UX paradigms guiding Audi's digital design.
description.pl: Sześć paradygmatów UX kierujących cyfrowym designem Audi.

principles.title: Personalization
principles.description: We personalize our service so as to provide each customer with an individual user experience. Habits, needs, individual mobility, personal devices, security and privacy: all these differ from one user to the next. So we enable users to change or supplement content according to their individual preferences.

principles.title: Context
principles.description: Users can choose individually from a range of different interests, positions and objectives. They may also take on different roles such as potential customer, buyer or owner. To create a positive experience, it is important to understand and incorporate the needs and aims of the user in the design.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: We use a clear visual language to users on all channels and offer recurring solutions. Entire sets of content, hierarchies and functions are structured identically across all devices. We give functions the same name and apply animations in the same way.

principles.title: Clarity
principles.description: Clear terms in unambiguous language help establish clarity when performing a task. We focus on the essentials and guide the user through particular highlights and animations by means of a clear-cut hierarchy.

principles.title: Reliability
principles.description: Transparency and data protection are very important to the user. Since more and more services are interconnected across different systems and devices, the user has to be able to rely on every element in the ecosystem.

principles.title: Details
principles.description: Details are not optional: they are a fundamental component of our visual appearance. We apply details such as animations selectively so as to create a high-quality, thrilling and hallmark overall user experience.

description.en: Nine principles for fast, bold, scalable design.
description.pl: Dziewięć zasad szybkiego, odważnego, skalowalnego designu.

principles.title: Delight with speed
principles.description: Use design to make our products feel fast and responsive.

principles.title: Keep it fresh
principles.description: Use bold, high-contrast designs to bring focus and clarity to key actions or information, and to represent BuzzFeed's youthful brand.

principles.title: Know the goals
principles.description: When designing, whether in sketches, wireframes or multiple high-fidelity options, our work should always reflect the product goals.

principles.title: Consider the ecosystem
principles.description: Design modules and write copy with an awareness of all the places they may show up, as well as which types of BuzzFeed content they may appear with.

principles.title: Design with the platform
principles.description: Balance native platform elements and patterns with BuzzFeed's own design patterns and content. Our products should behave natively, while remaining uniquely BuzzFeed.

principles.title: Advocate for our users
principles.description: It's our responsibility to understand our users' needs, as well as to advocate for them with our teams and in our work.

principles.title: Pair simplicity with delight
principles.description: Design purposeful interfaces that favor usability, while also infusing delight through color, animation and language.

principles.title: Design for scale
principles.description: Design with an eye toward the future of our products. Value flexible, scalable designs that can quickly evolve alongside our content.

principles.title: Learn, learn again
principles.description: Know the data surrounding your product well enough to discuss, describe and deeply inform your design work. Constantly validate your ideas through A/B testing or qualitative analysis.

description.en: Six principles from the US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
description.pl: Sześć zasad amerykańskiego biura ochrony konsumenta finansowego.

principles.title: Public service, public trust
principles.description: Build trust through honest, transparent design that is always consumer-driven. Demonstrate openness through user-friendly experiences and open-source content.

principles.title: Give the user control
principles.description: Empower users with information to make their own financial decisions. Provide all necessary information succinctly and let consumers decide how to use it.

principles.title: Aesthetic integrity
principles.description: Align appearance with purpose. Good design integrates form and function, creating a trustworthy tone through clear and intuitive interfaces.

principles.title: Design with data
principles.description: Let data inform design decisions and use design to make complex data understandable. Visualisation gives voice to otherwise indigestible numbers.

principles.title: Inclusion and accessibility
principles.description: Design for the widest possible audience with plain language and intuitive interfaces. Meet each user where they are, regardless of skill level.

principles.title: Coherent end-to-end user experience
principles.description: Guide users seamlessly from beginning to end. Navigation should be intuitive and transitions smooth, with consistent quality throughout.

description.en: Six principles emphasising context, honesty, and openness.
description.pl: Sześć zasad podkreślających kontekst, uczciwość i otwartość.

principles.title: We design in context
principles.description: Communicate with a clear voice at the right time. Understand the whole user experience, not just the digital part, and give information only when needed.

principles.title: We design with purpose
principles.description: Know why a service is needed before building it. Get out of the way and help users achieve their goals as quickly as possible.

principles.title: We design for everyone
principles.description: Communicate simply and remove barriers. Design for people regardless of background, circumstance, or digital skills.

principles.title: We design with honesty
principles.description: Be truthful about what you can and cannot do. Talk about what you've done, not what you've yet to do.

principles.title: We design in the open
principles.description: Share what you're making as you make it. Be generous with knowledge and open to learning from others.

principles.title: We design iteratively
principles.description: Release earlier and learn faster. Make decisions based on evidence from what people actually do, not what they say.

description.en: Four principles for delightful, transitional interfaces.

principles.title: Interaction is the basic unit of design
principles.description: Begin the design process by identifying the user's origin point, their goal, and the steps in between. A successful design makes every step along the way clear while keeping the user focused on their goal.

principles.title: Transitional interfaces are easier to learn and more pleasant to use
principles.description: Take advantage of animation and conditional visibility to guide users between steps and to add rhythm and momentum to interactions.

principles.title: Interactions should be delightful and surprising
principles.description: Design these interactions so that they're enjoyable to perform again and again. Minimize the effort required to complete tasks, enable users to recover from mistakes, and ensure that they receive feedback after taking any action.

principles.title: Focus the user on one primary action at a time
principles.description: Avoid sidebars, widgets, and multi-column layouts. Rather than confronting the user with a multitude of possibilities, use visual hierarchy to help users make meaningful decisions and allow actions to unfold across multiple steps. At the same time, be sure to make it easy for the user to move efficiently between primary actions in case they need to change gears.

description.en: Six principles for the LINE messaging app design system.
description.pl: Sześć zasad systemu designu komunikatora LINE.

principles.title: WE ≠ USERS
principles.description: As designers, we are not the main target of our designs. We must investigate what users actually need rather than assuming they share our perspectives.

principles.title: Clear primary tasks
principles.description: Make primary tasks intuitive so users can perform important tasks without overthinking, as users gauge LINE on functionality beyond aesthetics.

principles.title: Chat comes first
principles.description: LINE's first priority is enabling conversations between people, with new features designed to reinforce the core chat experience.

principles.title: Reliable design
principles.description: Pursue trustworthy design that is intuitive for all ages across multiple use cases, maintaining LINE's aesthetic standards.

principles.title: A cohesive experience
principles.description: Strive to provide a singular, consistent experience across screens, ensuring seamless flow that considers context and relationships between screens.

principles.title: Respect for legacy
principles.description: Respect what's already there and phase in changes appropriately, as users may have unexpected usage patterns or familiarity with existing UX.

description.en: Four principles for products that work for everyone.
description.pl: Cztery zasady projektowania produktów dla każdego.

principles.title: Good design works for everyone
principles.description: Designing for edge cases improves the experience for all users. Subtitles help in noisy environments, plain language aids experts too, and large click targets benefit everyone.

principles.title: Good design makes things obvious
principles.description: The best solutions feel inevitable. Show navigation items instead of hiding them in hamburger menus, display hints inline rather than in tooltips.

principles.title: Good design puts users in control
principles.description: Design for real life, not ideal workflows. Let users save progress, trigger menus on click not hover, and paginate instead of infinite scroll.

principles.title: Good design is lightweight
principles.description: Slow interfaces cause stress and feel untrustworthy. Cut background videos, remove unnecessary tooltips, and show content inline instead of in carousels.

description.en: Ten content design principles from Bristol City Council.
description.pl: Dziesięć zasad projektowania treści Bristol City Council.

principles.title: Think about whether the content needs to be on our site
principles.description: Only add content when there's clear user demand, legal obligation, or Bristol-specific information that people need to know before taking regulated actions or complying with statutory requirements.

principles.title: Put the user first
principles.description: Prioritise user needs and perspectives when creating content, ensuring that every piece of information serves a genuine purpose for Bristol residents accessing council services.

principles.title: Create content that everyone can use
principles.description: Design content with accessibility at the forefront, ensuring that all users regardless of ability can access and understand council information and services.

principles.title: Be inclusive
principles.description: Use language and design approaches that welcome and represent Bristol's diverse community, ensuring no one feels excluded from accessing council services and information.

principles.title: Encourage trust
principles.description: Build confidence through reliable, accurate, and transparent content that helps residents trust the council as a source of authoritative information and services.

principles.title: Be clear and to the point
principles.description: Communicate information directly and concisely, avoiding unnecessary complexity while ensuring residents can quickly understand what they need to know and do.

principles.title: Structure your content
principles.description: Organise information logically with clear headings, sections, and navigation patterns that help users find what they need efficiently and understand relationships between topics.

principles.title: Use an active, balanced tone of voice
principles.description: Write in an active voice that sounds approachable yet professional, maintaining a balanced tone that reflects the council's role as a public service provider.

principles.title: Think about how words are pronounced
principles.description: Choose words and phrases that are easy to read and understand, particularly for people with reading difficulties or those using screen readers to access council content.

principles.title: Use our A to Z of style
principles.description: Follow the council's established style guide consistently to maintain coherence across all content and ensure professional presentation of council information.

description.en: Six principles of the Brainly Pencil design system.

principles.title: Personality on Brand
principles.description: Design interactions and visuals that clearly reflect the brand's character, tone, and identity so the experience feels recognisable and authentic.

principles.title: Effortless Experience
principles.description: Create a smooth, intuitive experience that works reliably across devices and platforms with minimal friction or errors.

principles.title: Necessary Things Only
principles.description: Focus on what truly matters by removing unnecessary elements so users can complete tasks quickly and without distraction.

principles.title: Consistent & Connected
principles.description: Maintain consistent patterns, language, and structure so users can move through the product confidently without relearning how things work.

principles.title: Inclusive of Everybody
principles.description: Design for a wide range of people, abilities, and contexts so the product is accessible and usable for as many users as possible.

principles.title: Legible Value
principles.description: Make the value of the product and each design decision clear, transparent, and easy for users to understand.

description.en: Eight principles by Amber Case for unobtrusive, peripheral technology.
description.pl: Osiem zasad Amber Case o nienachalnej, peryferyjnej technologii.

principles.title: Technology should require the smallest possible amount of attention
principles.description: Communicate information without pulling users out of their environment or task. Create ambient awareness through different senses.

principles.title: Technology should inform and create calm
principles.description: A person's primary task should not be computing, but being human. Give people what they need to solve their problem, and nothing more.

principles.title: Technology should make use of the periphery
principles.description: Calm technology moves easily from the periphery of attention to the centre and back. The periphery informs without overburdening.

principles.title: Technology should amplify the best of technology and the best of humanity
principles.description: Design for people first. Machines shouldn't act like humans, and humans shouldn't act like machines. Amplify the best of each.

principles.title: Technology can communicate, but doesn't need to speak
principles.description: Consider whether your product needs voice or can use a different communication method. Think about how technology communicates status.

principles.title: Technology should work even when it fails
principles.description: Consider what happens when your technology fails. Does it default to a usable state or break down completely?

principles.title: The right amount of technology is the minimum needed to solve the problem
principles.description: Slim the feature set down so the product does what it needs to do and no more. Question every addition.

principles.title: Technology should respect social norms
principles.description: Technology takes time to introduce. Consider what social norms your product might violate. Leverage familiar behaviours to introduce new ones.

description.en: Thirteen design principles behind the React UI library.

principles.title: Composition
principles.description: Components written by different people should work well together, enabling functionality additions without causing rippling changes throughout the codebase.

principles.title: Common Abstraction
principles.description: Features implemented incompatibly or inefficiently across many components are baked into React itself to benefit the whole ecosystem.

principles.title: Escape Hatches
principles.description: Provide imperative APIs or temporary working solutions when useful patterns cannot be described declaratively, ensuring accessibility for developers of all skill levels.

principles.title: Stability
principles.description: Value API stability by studying internal usage, adding deprecation warnings, and backing out changes that are too early or require strategic preparation.

principles.title: Interoperability
principles.description: Enable gradual adoption and interoperability with existing systems, allowing teams to use React for small features without full rewrites.

principles.title: Scheduling
principles.description: Schedule and split work based on UI knowledge, prioritising user interactions over background work to avoid dropping frames and maintain responsiveness.

principles.title: Developer Experience
principles.description: Provide helpful developer warnings by understanding common mistakes internally and anticipating them when adding new features.

principles.title: Debugging
principles.description: Use props and state as breadcrumbs to trace UI mistakes to their source, ensuring state is available to React directly rather than trapped in closures.

principles.title: Configuration
principles.description: Avoid global runtime configuration options in code, keeping composition central to React's design.

principles.title: Beyond the DOM
principles.description: Maintain renderer-agnostic design to enable improvements across platforms and form engineering teams around products instead of platforms.

principles.title: Implementation
principles.description: Prefer boring, disposable code to clever abstractions, prioritising correctness, performance, and developer experience over elegance.

principles.title: Optimised for Tooling
principles.description: Use unique, verbose names to enable safe automated changes via codemods and easy custom lint rules without false positives.

principles.title: Dogfooding
principles.description: Prioritise internal Facebook usage to maintain sharp vision and focused direction, which counter-intuitively benefits the broader community.

description.en: Nine design principles from Canadian telco Telus.

principles.title: Clear and simple designs
principles.description: Promote the brand aesthetic. Reduce complexity by constraining choices. Ensure customers can complete task on first attempt. Leverage usability heuristics.

principles.title: Respect our customers
principles.description: Ensure decisions are informed by analytics and research. Designs should be accessible and usable to all. Don't hide information that customers need to achieve their goals.

principles.title: Support the business
principles.description: Balance business goals with customer needs. Design for scale.

principles.title: Be efficient
principles.description: Design with consistency by leveraging TDS. Look for similar design patterns first. All designs need to work within the platform.

principles.title: Measure
principles.description: Designs should have a measurable hypothesis. Leverage analytics. Test and iterate upon your designs.

principles.title: Mobile first
principles.description: Design for small screens first before moving onto large screens. Through responsive and adaptive design, ensure experiences are great across multiple screen sizes.

principles.title: Seek the perspective of others
principles.description: Collaborate by involving cross-functional team members. Ensure design is technically feasible and understand how it impacts performance. Share your ideas early and often to explore many different solutions and iterations.

principles.title: Think end-to-end
