principles.description: Experiences should move a customer towards their goal, leaving no dead ends. Support and enable multichannel experiences. Test the end-to-end experience to ensure continuity.

principles.title: Align with TELUS standards
principles.description: Accessibility. Privacy & Security. Performance. Brand. Content.

description.en: Fifteen principles for open-source, modular, sustainable building.
description.pl: Piętnaście zasad otwartego, modułowego, zrównoważonego budownictwa.

principles.title: Share global, manufacture local
principles.description: It is easier to ship recipes than cakes and biscuits – John Maynard Keynes

principles.title: Be lazy like a fox
principles.description: Don't keep reinventing the wheel. Take something that already works, copy, adapt, give credit and re-share. (Thanks Linus Torvalds via Eric S Raymond)

principles.title: Design to lower thresholds
principles.description: Design to lower barriers of time, cost, skill, energy and resources at every stage. Elvis Costello wrote all his songs to be played on the cheapest transistor radio.

principles.title: Share and make shareable
principles.description: Publish your work under an open source sharealike licence, documented and codified so as to make it as easy as possible for others to understand, modify, improve, distribute and use it, including commercially.

principles.title: Open standards
principles.description: Where possible, work to existing standards or seek to establish intuitive new ones.

principles.title: Open materials
principles.description: Design for cheap, abundant, standardised, sustainable, and, ideally, circular materials.

principles.title: Human friendly
principles.description: Seek to preserve and maximise the safety, security, health and wellbeing (physical and mental) of all participants at every stage of a product's life.

principles.title: Start somewhere
principles.description: No one can solve everyone's problems. Design something that works where you are, then share so others can adapt it for their own economy, climate and culture. Let solutions adapt like Darwin's finches.

principles.title: Modular
principles.description: Design hardware and software that is robust, interoperable, product-agnostic and flexible, so elements can be independently altered, substituted or upgraded.

principles.title: Include, keep including
principles.description: Look for ways in which age, race, gender or disability might be barriers, and try to design them out. Try to design products, processes and documents that are accessible, intuitive and non-discriminatory.

principles.title: The new 'normal'
principles.description: Avoid design which would be considered 'alternative', 'boutique' or only for the rich or poor. Instead, design for the new normal: products most people would consider desirable and affordable. As beautiful as Apple, as open as Linux.

principles.title: Mistake proof
principles.description: Make it impossible to get wrong, or not matter if you do. (The Japanese call this 'Poka-Yoke')

principles.title: Whole life design
principles.description: A home is not something you finish – Stewart Brand. Design for the entire life-cycle of the product, from manufacturing to assembly, use, maintenance, adaptation, disassembly and re-use.

principles.title: Superpower the users
principles.description: Give power to the fine tuners – Cedric Price. Afford as much power as possible to the end users, from procurement to privacy to electricity. Democracy is a design diagram.

principles.title: If you can't mend it, you don't own it
principles.description: Try to avoid 'black box' products. Try to make it easy for the user to learn how it works.

description.en: Seven snappy manifesto rules from a Berlin design agency.
description.pl: Siedem zwięzłych zasad berlińskiego studia designu.

principles.title: We work for your customers.
principles.description: We may have to take their side at times.

principles.title: Challenge us.
principles.description: Complacency is the enemy of great work.

principles.title: We don't give answers.
principles.description: Unless we can explore your question.

principles.title: We are not suppliers
principles.description: Partnership gets the best results.

principles.title: Talk to us.
principles.description: We thrive on feedback.

principles.title: Trust us.
principles.description: You hired us because we do something you cannot.

principles.title: Pay us.
principles.description: Our work adds to your bottom line, so invest in our future.

description.en: Five principles for heirloom-quality lifestyle products.
description.pl: Pięć zasad lifestyle'owych produktów o jakości heirloom.

principles.title: Use Less And Do More
principles.description: We're always looking for ways to use less and do more. Less material and fewer cuts with more ways to use it, more ways to share it, and more ways to repurpose or recycle it.

principles.title: Create An Heirloom
principles.description: We design our products to stand the test of time, not only in their material life but in their aesthetic as well. Objects you can be proud to pass down, and those that equally excite future generations.

principles.title: Produce With A Craftsman's Sprit
principles.description: It's not just what's on the outside but what's on the inside that defines an object. Clean bindings, neat stitches, and elegant backs show the depth of craft in an object.

principles.title: Design For The Heart
principles.description: An object should be appreciated by the mind as well as the heart. Charm and character makes it unique when compared to the same functional object. It's what makes you pause and smile.

principles.title: Look Back And Think Forward
principles.description: We look to new materials and methods of production to improve quality while reducing our impact. Looking back and thinking forward - learning from the longest lasting ecosystem: our planet.

description.en: Seventeen UX rules from Moo.com (circa 2008).

principles.title: Optimise for the common case
principles.description: Adding features for a small number of users confuses everyone else. Build for the majority first.

principles.title: Build tools that focus on meeting one simple need
principles.description: Each tool should do one thing well. Complexity comes from combining simple tools, not building complicated ones.

principles.title: Build tools for users without experience
principles.description: Design for people who've never used the product before. Experienced users will figure it out.

principles.title: Users needs are not always the same as the features they ask for
principles.description: Listen to what users are trying to achieve, not the specific solutions they suggest.

principles.title: One action per page
principles.description: Each page should have one clear purpose. Multiple competing actions create confusion.

principles.title: Context is more important than consistency
principles.description: What works in one situation may not work in another. Adapt to context rather than forcing uniformity.

principles.title: Optimise for average user's return rate
principles.description: Design for how often typical users actually come back, not power users or one-time visitors.

principles.title: Make pages functionally readable
principles.description: Users should understand what a page does at a glance. Structure content for scanning.

principles.title: Only tell people things once per page
principles.description: Repeating information wastes attention. Say it once, clearly, in the right place.

principles.title: Contextual help is best
principles.description: Help should appear where and when it's needed, not hidden in separate documentation.

principles.title: Let people teach themselves
principles.description: Design interfaces that are learnable through exploration rather than requiring instruction.

principles.title: Keep the user path as short as possible
principles.description: Every extra step is a chance to lose someone. Remove unnecessary pages and clicks.

principles.title: Make decisions for people
principles.description: Good defaults reduce cognitive load. Only ask users to decide when it genuinely matters.

principles.title: Make people confident in their actions
principles.description: Users should feel certain about what will happen before they click. Remove ambiguity.

principles.title: Pages make sense before and after action
principles.description: The page state should be clear whether the user has just arrived or just completed something.

principles.title: State should always be maintained between pages
principles.description: Never lose user progress when they navigate. Preserve their work and selections.

principles.title: Make sure pages content can be linked to forever
principles.description: URLs should be permanent. If pages must be removed, redirect to somewhere useful.

description.en: Nine ethics-led principles from the Orange Design System.
description.pl: Dziewięć zasad etyki w designie Orange.

principles.title: Interdependency
principles.description: The principles are interdependent and related to each other, with the realization of one principle often depending on the successful realization of others, constructing an overall ethical vision.

principles.title: Health
principles.description: Protect physical, mental, and social health by conducting risk assessments, ergonomic design, preventing addiction and abuse, and respecting people's time and attention as finite resources.

principles.title: Service
principles.description: Serve users by understanding their expectations and obstacles, creating products that respond to proven needs rather than pushing technology or following market trends.

principles.title: Trust
principles.description: Earn trust through consent by never using dark patterns or manipulation tricks, valuing users as ends in themselves, and helping them identify manipulation elsewhere.

principles.title: Stakeholders
principles.description: Consider all stakeholders including users, suppliers, partners, shareholders, society, and future generations, evaluating impacts on direct and indirect stakeholders.

principles.title: Planet
principles.description: Regenerate the planet's living systems by examining lifecycle ecological impact, prioritising regeneration over sustainability, and creating recyclable, repairable, and improvable products.

principles.title: Agency
principles.description: Provide keys to free and informed use by balancing usability and control, ensuring technology serves humans, and making products explainable in approachable ways.

principles.title: Inclusivity
principles.description: Design for all by finding the right balance between simplicity and user control, ensuring technology serves humans and not the inverse, with fair data exchanges.

principles.title: Value
principles.description: Create value for the company, humans and life by integrating economic, social, and environmental value, generating co-benefits and accounting for ecosystem services.

description.en: Six principles of the Škoda Flow design system.

principles.title: Caring
principles.description: Put people at the centre of everything. Provide helpful guidance that adapts to user needs, keeping options visible and reducing cognitive load through minimalist aesthetics.

principles.title: Immersive
principles.description: Empower users to feel confident and in control. Provide tools and information for informed decisions, prioritising usability over fancy effects.

principles.title: Creative
principles.description: Stimulate curiosity and imagination with original angles. Create digital experiences that leave users both satisfied and inspired through considered aesthetics.

principles.title: Bold
principles.description: Define experiences through actions, not descriptions. Never settle for plain or neutral—seek surprising angles whilst maintaining clear hierarchy of usability and purpose.

principles.title: Fulfilling
principles.description: Create a sense of achievement and contentment. Build positive feedback and responsiveness into the UX so users feel delight when tasks are completed.

principles.title: Fluid
principles.description: Make digital experiences effortless and frictionless. Break complex tasks into simple steps, ensuring both novices and experts can find their way around.

description.en: Five design system principles from DocPlanner's Watson.
description.pl: Pięć zasad systemu Watson od DocPlanner.

principles.title: Unified & Holistic
principles.description: The design system serves as the single source of truth, ensuring predictable and cohesive experiences across all products while respecting platform-specific conventions.

principles.title: Designed to Evolve
principles.description: The design system is a living product that embraces continuous improvement through modular components that can be added, deprecated, and updated without breaking changes.

principles.title: Intentional and Opinionated
principles.description: The system makes thoughtful, deliberate choices to simplify decision-making and maintain high standards of quality across the entire ecosystem.

principles.title: Committed to Quality
principles.description: The design system is held to a high standard as the foundation for all products, ensuring reliability, efficiency, and scalability.

principles.title: Collaborative
principles.description: The design system is built for its community, encouraging teams to both utilise existing components and actively contribute to its evolution.

description.en: Fourteen principles from the Zen of GitHub.

principles.title: Responsive is better than fast
principles.description: Design for all users and contexts rather than optimizing for speed at the expense of accessibility and inclusivity.

principles.title: It's not fully shipped until it's fast
principles.description: Performance is not an afterthought; features must be performant to be considered complete.

principles.title: Anything added dilutes everything else
principles.description: Every addition to the interface increases cognitive load; be intentional about what you include.

principles.title: Practicality beats purity
principles.description: Choose solutions that work in practice over theoretically perfect but impractical approaches.

principles.title: Approachable is better than simple
principles.description: Design should be welcoming and easy to understand, not just technically simple.

principles.title: Mind your words, they are important
principles.description: Language and communication are critical to user experience and understanding.

principles.title: Speak like a human
principles.description: Use natural, human language in interfaces and documentation.

principles.title: Half measures are as bad as nothing at all
principles.description: Commit fully to solutions; partial implementations create more problems than they solve.

principles.title: Encourage flow
principles.description: Design experiences that allow users to maintain focus and productivity without interruption.

principles.title: Non-blocking is better than blocking
principles.description: Avoid preventing users from continuing their work; design for asynchronous workflows.

principles.title: Favor focus over features
principles.description: Prioritize helping users accomplish their goals over adding unnecessary features.

principles.title: Avoid administrative distraction
principles.description: Minimize overhead and administrative tasks that distract from primary work.

principles.title: Design for failure
principles.description: Anticipate and handle errors gracefully; systems should be resilient.

principles.title: Keep it logically awesome
principles.description: Maintain clear, logical structure and reasoning in design decisions.

description.en: Eight principles from the makers of Basecamp.

principles.title: Useful is forever
principles.description: Bells and whistles wear off, but usefulness never does. We build useful software that does just what you need and nothing you don't.

principles.title: Great service is everything
principles.description: We're famous for fast and friendly customer service. We work hard to make sure we live up to that reputation every day.

principles.title: Clarity is king
principles.description: Buzzwords, lingo, and sensationalized sales-and-marketing-speak have no place at 37signals. We communicate clearly and honestly.

principles.title: Our customers are our investors
principles.description: Our customers fund our daily operations by paying for our products. We answer to them — not investors, the stock market, or a board of directors.

principles.title: The basics are beautiful
principles.description: We'll never overlook what really matters: The basics. Great service, ease of use, honest pricing, and respect for our customer's time, money, and trust.

principles.title: No hidden fees or secret prices
principles.description: We believe everyone is entitled to the best price we can offer. Our prices are public, published right on our site, and the same no matter who you are.

principles.title: Software should be easy
principles.description: Our products are intuitive. You'll pick them up in seconds or minutes, not hours, days or weeks. We don't sell you training because you don't need it.

principles.title: Long-term contracts are obscene
principles.description: No one likes being locked into something they don't want anymore. Our customers can cancel at any time, no questions asked. No setup/termination fees either.

description.en: Five principles from the Autodesk Human Interface Guidelines.
description.pl: Pięć zasad z Human Interface Guidelines Autodesk.

principles.title: Put customers first
principles.description: Understand who uses the product and what they're trying to achieve. Design decisions should flow from customer needs, not internal convenience.

principles.title: Connected and interconnected
principles.description: Products should work together as part of a larger ecosystem. Data and workflows should flow seamlessly between tools.

principles.title: Adapt and grow
principles.description: Design for change and evolution. Products should accommodate different skill levels and grow with users as their needs develop.

principles.title: Make the complex beautifully clear
principles.description: Professional tools handle complex tasks, but complexity shouldn't mean confusion. Present information clearly and reduce cognitive load.

principles.title: Distinctively Autodesk
principles.description: Maintain a consistent identity across products while respecting each tool's unique purpose. Users should recognise the Autodesk experience.

description.en: Six experience principles from the Mendeley research platform.

principles.title: Empowered
principles.description: Where we can, we should inspire creativity in their workflow, and inspire new ways of researcher thinking through content discovery.

principles.title: Confident
principles.description: Our users are tackling the world's biggest problems. Where we can, we should inspire trust in our content and data.

principles.title: Considered
principles.description: Our users are inundated with content. Let's be as relevant and helpful to them on an individual basis as we can.

principles.title: Organised
principles.description: Our users have so much to keep on top of. Where we can, let's bring order to the madness.

principles.title: Calm
principles.description: Our users have such a disconnected workflow. We should help them out with this and connect the dots where we can.

principles.title: Connected
principles.description: Our users should feel like they are 'standing on the shoulders of giants', that they're part of a bigger picture, and that they can connect with people from across the world.

description.en: Six design principles from Nordhealth.

principles.title: Put user needs first
principles.description: Care for the people who use products by making their day-to-day and long-term work better and more pleasant through great user experience.

principles.title: Strive for consistency, not uniformity
principles.description: Use the same language and design patterns wherever possible to help people get familiar with services, while holding true for the system and developer experience.

principles.title: Default to openness
principles.description: Share what is being done whenever possible, building services transparently to increase visibility and accountability while pushing towards higher quality.

principles.title: Make it accessible
principles.description: Ensure services are for everyone by making sure people with different needs can use products and meet WCAG 2.1 accessibility standards.

principles.title: Provide a good developer experience
principles.description: Enable developers to start using tools in minutes rather than hours, days, or weeks, prioritising efficient onboarding and implementation.

principles.title: Automate everything you can
principles.description: Value the time of colleagues, users, and future selves by proactively looking for ways to automate repetitive tasks and testing.

description.en: Eight golden rules of interface design — a foundational HCI text.
description.pl: Osiem złotych zasad projektowania interfejsów — fundamentalny tekst HCI.

principles.title: Strive for consistency
principles.description: Consistent sequences of actions should be required in similar situations; identical terminology should be used in prompts, menus, and help screens; and consistent commands should be employed throughout.

principles.title: Enable frequent users to use shortcuts
principles.description: As the frequency of use increases, so do the user's desires to reduce the number of interactions and to increase the pace of interaction. Abbreviations, function keys, hidden commands, and macro facilities are very helpful to an expert user.

principles.title: Offer informative feedback
principles.description: For every operator action, there should be some system feedback. For frequent and minor actions, the response can be modest, while for infrequent and major actions, the response should be more substantial.

principles.title: Design dialog to yield closure
principles.description: Sequences of actions should be organized into groups with a beginning, middle, and end. The informative feedback at the completion of a group of actions gives the operators the satisfaction of accomplishment, a sense of relief, the signal to drop contingency plans and options from their minds, and an indication that the way is clear to prepare for the next group of actions.

principles.title: Offer simple error handling
principles.description: As much as possible, design the system so the user cannot make a serious error. If an error is made, the system should be able to detect the error and offer simple, comprehensible mechanisms for handling the error.

principles.title: Permit easy reversal of actions
principles.description: This feature relieves anxiety, since the user knows that errors can be undone; it thus encourages exploration of unfamiliar options. The units of reversibility may be a single action, a data entry, or a complete group of actions.

principles.title: Support internal locus of control
principles.description: Experienced operators strongly desire the sense that they are in charge of the system and that the system responds to their actions. Design the system to make users the initiators of actions rather than the responders.

principles.title: Reduce short-term memory load
principles.description: The limitation of human information processing in short-term memory requires that displays be kept simple, multiple page displays be consolidated, window-motion frequency be reduced, and sufficient training time be allotted for codes, mnemonics, and sequences of actions.

description.en: Four motion principles from Sprout Social's Seeds design system.
description.pl: Cztery zasady motion z Seeds Sprout Social.

principles.title: Integrity
principles.description: Progress the story forward whilst maintaining design consistency. Each element should be as strong as the last throughout any transition.

principles.title: Intentionality
principles.description: Every action must have a motivation. There should always be a clear reason for why something behaves the way it does.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: Elements should operate within a consistent set of rules. These don't have to mirror the real world, but must follow the system's established patterns.

principles.title: Emotional Appeal
principles.description: All elements should work in concert to evoke an emotional experience through surprise, delight, and thoughtful details.

description.en: Five principles of the U.S. Web Design System.
description.pl: Pięć zasad U.S. Web Design System.

principles.title: Make the best thing the easiest thing
principles.description: Provide the easiest path for federal teams to comply with policy through open-source, mobile-first code and assets.

principles.title: Offer accessibility out of the box
principles.description: Every asset meets Section 508 accessibility standards, with guidance for compliant customisations.

principles.title: Design for flexibility
principles.description: Patterns adapt to diverse government needs, focusing on performance and user validation.

principles.title: Showcase benefits for agency and users
principles.description: Catalogue successes to inspire teams and support the business case for adoption.

principles.title: Reuse, reuse, reuse
principles.description: Provide tried-and-true components so teams can focus on unique aspects rather than recreating basics.

description.en: Ten principles of effective web design by the Smashing Mag founder.
description.pl: Dziesięć zasad skutecznego web designu od założyciela Smashing Mag.

principles.title: Don't Make Users Think
principles.description: Make web pages obvious and self-explanatory. Reduce question marks through clear structure, visual clues, and recognizable links.

principles.title: Don't Squander Users' Patience
principles.description: Keep user requirements minimal. Remove barriers and don't force registrations before users can explore and test features.

principles.title: Manage To Focus Users' Attention
principles.description: Use visual elements strategically to guide attention to specific areas. Less thinking behind scenes means better user experience.

principles.title: Strive For Feature Exposure
principles.description: Make functions clearly visible through visually appealing 1-2-3-done steps and large buttons. Well-understood content makes users comfortable.

principles.title: Make Use Of Effective Writing
principles.description: Use short, scannable phrases with plain, objective language. Avoid cute names, marketing jargon, and exaggerated statements.

principles.title: Strive For Simplicity
principles.description: Keep it simple as the primary goal. Users look for information despite design, not because of it. Simplicity over complexity.

principles.title: Don't Be Afraid Of The White Space
principles.description: Use whitespace to reduce cognitive load and help users perceive information. Hierarchical structures with whitespace are easier to scan.

principles.title: Communicate Effectively With A Visible Language
principles.description: Organize with clear structure, economize with minimal cues, and communicate matching user capabilities. Use max 3 typefaces and sizes.

principles.title: Conventions Are Our Friends
principles.description: Follow established conventions to reduce learning curve and gain user confidence. Innovate only when you have a better idea.

principles.title: Test Early, Test Often
principles.description: Apply the TETO-principle to every project. Testing one user early is better than testing 50 near the end. Testing is iterative.

description.en: Six design principles from Westpac's Global Experience Language.
description.pl: Sześć zasad Global Experience Language Westpac.

principles.title: Customer centricity
principles.description: Across our business, everything we do starts with the customer at the centre. It means every single process and every single practice should be built from the customer's perspective.

principles.title: CX design
principles.description: Our CX design principles will help your solutions reflect the core expectations for our customers and brands.

principles.title: Responsive Design
principles.description: Only with a thorough understanding of why responsive design is the right approach can you confidently influence the project to do the right thing by our customers in adopting it.

principles.title: Accessibility
principles.description: We should always practice inclusive design. Your design solutions should be AA compliant with WCAG 2.0 guidelines. This is both a social obligation and a legal requirement.

principles.title: Multi-brand
principles.description: We're a multi-brand organisation. We need to be smarter in the way we think about design, re-using wherever possible to achieve more with less effort.

principles.title: Our values
principles.description: We don't just pay lip service to the concept of values we take our values seriously. They have real, practical relevance to your work and workplace.

description.en: Five principles for user-centred government from the Netherlands.
description.pl: Pięć zasad rządu skoncentrowanego na użytkowniku z Holandii.

principles.title: User central
principles.description: Design out of needs and context of people, not technology or organization

principles.title: Only be satisfied when your user is
principles.description: Design, test, measure and improve. And continue to do so.

principles.title: Make it easy for the user
principles.description: Design simple processes, create user-friendly systems and write understandable

principles.title: Use facts, not assumptions
principles.description: Base design on facts and usability research, do not assume the user is like you

principles.title: Be open and share your knowledge
principles.description: Collaborate and share your knowledge and experience. And welcome feedback.

description.en: Five AI design principles from Google PAIR (People + AI Research).
description.pl: Pięć zasad designu AI od Google PAIR.

principles.title: User Autonomy
principles.description: Design for the appropriate level of user autonomy in AI-supported workflows, considering different user tasks, expertise, and the effort required to steer the AI system.

principles.title: Data & Model Alignment
principles.description: Align datasets and models with people's real-world interactions with AI systems, accounting for unexpected tasks and contexts that may emerge as the product scales.

principles.title: Evolving Safety
principles.description: Treat safety as an evolving endeavor with multifaceted strategies that adapt to changing technology, user contexts, and complexity over time.

principles.title: Adapt with Feedback
principles.description: Create bidirectional feedback loops where AI learns from users to personalize experiences, and users adapt their behaviors in response to AI outcomes.

principles.title: Helpful AI
principles.description: Create AI experiences that enhance aspects of work and play that people enjoy, focusing on seamless integration and inspiration rather than just efficiency gains.

description.en: Five AI principles from Red Hat's PatternFly design system.
description.pl: Pięć zasad AI z PatternFly Red Hat.

principles.title: Accountability
principles.description: Take responsibility for AI systems and their outcomes, ensuring proper oversight and governance throughout the design and development process.

principles.title: Explainability
principles.description: Make AI decision-making processes understandable, allowing users and stakeholders to comprehend how and why AI reaches its conclusions.

principles.title: Transparency
principles.description: Be open about when AI is being used, its capabilities and limitations, and how it makes decisions. Keep users informed and in control.

principles.title: Fairness
principles.description: Design AI systems that treat all users equitably, actively working to identify and mitigate bias in data, algorithms, and outcomes.

principles.title: Human-centeredness
principles.description: Ensure AI enhances rather than replaces human abilities. Nurture collaboration, welcome multiple perspectives, and always validate AI output for accuracy.

description.en: Eight principles for the agentic enterprise from Salesforce.
description.pl: Osiem zasad agentic enterprise od Salesforce.

principles.title: Design for modularity
principles.description: Build reusable, composable components that can be reconfigured for different agent functions without rebuilding entire architecture elements from scratch.

principles.title: Harmonise data with metadata-driven understanding
principles.description: Provide agents with unified data and metadata, business glossaries, and ontologies so they can understand context and make informed decisions across systems.

principles.title: Enable unified observability
principles.description: Maintain real-time visibility into agent actions, reasoning, context, governance, and business outcomes across both IT and business functions.

principles.title: Build with trust
principles.description: Embed governance and trust principles throughout the architecture, including agent identities, task-based permissions, and policy compliance checks.

principles.title: Design for strategic human intervention and oversight
principles.description: Implement appropriate human-in-the-loop engagement at decision points, with smooth handoffs that preserve context when escalation is needed.

principles.title: Enable event-driven processing
principles.description: Support real-time decision-making through always-on agents that respond to triggers across any channel, including texts, emails, calls, and APIs.

principles.title: Ensure infrastructure can scale growing AI workloads
principles.description: Build resilient infrastructure with compute that scales based on workload needs, distributed loads, and storage that handles unpredictable data access patterns.

principles.title: Prioritise open ecosystems and standards
principles.description: Design for interoperability using standard interfaces, open protocols, and portable workflow definitions to avoid vendor lock-in and enable flexibility.

description.en: Four principles from personalised storybook makers Wonderbly.
description.pl: Cztery zasady twórców personalizowanych książek Wonderbly.

principles.title: Be Storytellers
principles.description: Everything should feel like part of a story. The experience of creating a personalised book should be as magical as reading one.

principles.title: Join Our Club
principles.description: Make customers feel part of something special. Build community and belonging around the shared experience of giving personalised gifts.

principles.title: Optimized Experiences
principles.description: Design for performance and efficiency. Fast, smooth experiences show respect for users' time and build trust in the product.

principles.title: Grandma First
principles.description: Design for the least technically confident user. If grandma can complete the purchase without help, everyone can.

description.en: Six principles from a French gardening app, full of garden poetry.
description.pl: Sześć zasad francuskiej aplikacji ogrodniczej, pełnych poezji ogrodu.

principles.title: Less is more
principles.description: Groww puts garden advice – the right information, simple and concise – at your fingertips, right when you need it.

principles.title: Grow my garden, grow myself up
principles.description: Growing your garden is also growing yourself up – learning new things!

principles.title: Gardening is a journey
principles.description: Gardening is a school of patience : you learn from the past – and your mistakes – to prepare the future. It's also a story you write, everyday.

principles.title: Stronger together
principles.description: Gardening is not something you do in your own – gardening is about sharing and exchanging ideas.

principles.title: We're outdoor folks
principles.description: Let's be clear – gardening is not something you do in front of your computer – you have to put your hands in the dirt. Groww is in your phone – ready to help, but the more the phone stays in the front pocket of your gardening apron, the better.

principles.title: No spray
principles.description: We do not want pesticides, herbicides, or any other '-cides' (from latin -cida, to kill) in Groww. We don't put any in our gardens, and there is no reason to do otherwise in this app! And beyond: in the garden we should use local ressources – mulch from our clippings instead of cacao beans from the other side of the world, and try reuse and recycle everything that can be used again. This planet is our garden!

description.en: Four design principles for HTML from the W3C.
description.pl: Cztery zasady projektowe HTML z W3C.

principles.title: Compatibility
principles.description: Address the necessity of supporting existing HTML content, design HTML 5 document requirements so that Web content can degrade gradually; and specify, adopt and adapt existing technology where possible.

principles.title: Utility
principles.description: The principles of utility call for design that ensures features can be used effectively, and for all intended purposes.

principles.title: Interoperability
principles.description: Interoperable HTML 5 implementation means defining behaviors in preference to vague or implementation-define behavior, avoiding needless complexity, and handling errors gracefully as opposed to hard failure.

principles.title: Universal access
principles.description: Features should be designed for universal access - to work across as many platforms as possible, support all world languages and scripts, and to be accessible to all users, including those with disabilities.

description.en: Five principles of the Lean Startup methodology.

principles.title: Entrepreneurs Are Everywhere
principles.description: You don't have to work in a garage to be in a startup.

principles.title: Entrepreneurship Is Management
principles.description: A startup is an institution, not just a product, so it requires management, a new kind of management specifically geared to its context.

principles.title: Validated Learning
principles.description: Startups exist not to make stuff, make money, or serve customers. They exist to learn how to build a sustainable business. This learning can be validated scientifically, by running experiments that allow us to test each element of our vision.

principles.title: Innovation Accounting
principles.description: To improve entrepreneurial outcomes, and to hold entrepreneurs accountable, we need to focus on the boring stuff: how to measure progress, how to setup milestones, how to prioritize work. This requires a new kind of accounting, specific to startups.

principles.title: Build-Measure-Learn
principles.description: The fundamental activity of a startup is to turn ideas into products, measure how customers respond, and then learn whether to pivot or persevere. All successful startup processes should be geared to accelerate that feedback loop.

description.en: Five principles from the Dutch railways Tractie design system.
description.pl: Pięć zasad systemu Tractie holenderskich kolei.

principles.title: Match purpose and context
principles.description: NS systems support specific roles and functions, caring about diverse and changeable contexts like location, time, profile, urgency, and weather to ensure users can accomplish tasks in any situation.

principles.title: Respect craftsmanship
principles.description: Craftsmanship of the workforce is the starting point, with systems designed to support employee expertise and keep them in control through attention to details that show respect for their professionalism.

principles.title: Build trust in every interaction
principles.description: Users should rely on good user experiences regardless of task frequency or complexity, with trust built through every interaction and solid UX that maintains confidence in handling personal data.

principles.title: Make the complex beautifully clear
principles.description: Design systems to be as clear and simple as possible despite complex underlying processes, giving employees freedom to use systems optimally without limiting mandatory flows.

principles.title: Make the enterprise experience delightful
principles.description: Products should not only help perform tasks but also provide good feelings and motivation, looking at cohesion within the bigger picture and the entire employee journey beyond mere functionality.

description.en: Four design principles of the Salesforce Lightning Design System.

principles.title: Clarity
principles.description: Eliminate ambiguity and enable people to see, understand, and act with confidence.

principles.title: Efficiency
principles.description: Streamline and optimise workflows by intelligently anticipating needs to help people work better, smarter, and faster.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: Create familiarity and strengthen intuition by applying the same solution to the same problem.

principles.title: Beauty
principles.description: Demonstrate respect for people's time and attention through thoughtful and elegant craftsmanship.

description.en: Five principles of the Washington Post Design System.
description.pl: Pięć zasad systemu designu Washington Post.

principles.title: Reusable
principles.description: Design modular components that can be reused without modification. Maintain visual and functional consistency with comprehensive documentation.

principles.title: Functional
principles.description: Prioritise user needs and ensure every component serves a clear purpose. Optimise for performance and reliability across all use cases.

principles.title: Adaptable
principles.description: Ensure components provide optimal experience across screen sizes. Consider localisation and internationalisation for different languages and cultures.

principles.title: Predictable
principles.description: Maintain consistent design patterns to reduce cognitive load. Provide clear feedback and intuitive wayfinding so users can predict behaviour.

principles.title: Accessible
principles.description: Design to be usable by as many people as possible. Adhere to WCAG guidelines and use inclusive imagery and language.

description.en: Three top-level design principles for Android.

principles.title: Enchant Me
principles.description: Create moments of delight through beautiful visuals, thoughtful animations, and well-timed sounds. Make the experience feel magical and personal.

principles.title: Simplify My Life
principles.description: Keep things brief and use pictures instead of words where possible. Make decisions for users but let them have the final say.

principles.title: Make Me Amazing
principles.description: Help users feel capable by making complex tasks seem easy. Learn their preferences over time and suggest what they might want next.

description.en: Three questions shaping design at Australian real estate Domain.
description.pl: Trzy pytania kształtujące design Domain (australijska platforma nieruchomości).

principles.title: What Am I Solving?
principles.description: Effective designers are, at their core, great problem solvers. When kicking off a project it is up to us to first define the problem we are solving. If we don't understand what problem we are solving, how can we expect to design an effective solution to it?

principles.title: Do I Need This?
principles.description: This is a question we should be asking ourselves at every stage of the design process. Is this feature something the user wants or needs? Will this element improve usability? Does this help or hinder the user experience? Will the design still work without this element? We want designs that consist of everything the users need and nothing they don't. By constantly asking ourselves whether a bit of functionality or a design element is necessary, we are working towards that ideal.

principles.title: Where Is The Love?
principles.description: We are sometimes guilty of taking Minimum Viable Product to its extreme — stripping a product of everything loveable in the name of shipping fast. We want our users to love using our products, so we need to make sure that we deliver loveable products. Meet the Minimum Loveable Product.

description.en: Five toy-making principles from Fisher-Price founders.
description.pl: Pięć zasad projektowania zabawek założycieli Fisher-Price.

principles.title: Intrinsic play value
principles.description: Toys should engage children through inherent qualities that encourage exploration, imagination, and meaningful play experiences.

principles.title: Ingenuity
principles.description: Design should demonstrate creative problem-solving and innovative thinking that surprises and delights children.

principles.title: Strong construction
principles.description: Toys must be built to withstand active play, ensuring safety and longevity through robust materials and assembly.

principles.title: Good value for the money
principles.description: Products should offer quality and play value that justify their cost, making them accessible to families.

principles.title: Action
principles.description: Toys should incorporate movement, interaction, or dynamic elements that respond to a child's engagement.

description.en: Five principles of The Arch Way — Arch Linux philosophy.
description.pl: Pięć zasad The Arch Way — filozofii Arch Linuxa.

principles.title: Simplicity
principles.description: Arch Linux defines simplicity as without unnecessary additions or modifications. It ships software as released by the original developers (upstream) with minimal distribution-specific (downstream) changes. It does not add automation features such as enabling a service simply because the package was installed.

principles.title: Modernity
principles.description: Arch Linux strives to maintain the latest stable release versions of its software as long as systemic package breakage can be reasonably avoided. It is based on a rolling-release system, which allows a one-time installation with continuous upgrades.

principles.title: Pragmatism
principles.description: Arch is a pragmatic distribution rather than an ideological one. The principles here are only useful guidelines. Ultimately, design decisions are made on a case-by-case basis through developer consensus. Evidence-based technical analysis and debate are what matter, not politics or popular opinion.

principles.title: User centrality
principles.description: Whereas many GNU/Linux distributions attempt to be more user-friendly, Arch Linux has always been, and shall always remain user-centric. The distribution is intended to fill the needs of those contributing to it, rather than trying to appeal to as many users as possible. It is targeted at the proficient GNU/Linux user, or anyone with a do-it-yourself attitude who is willing to read the documentation, and solve their own problems.

principles.title: Versatility
principles.description: Arch Linux is a general-purpose distribution. Upon installation, only a command-line environment is provided: rather than tearing out unneeded and unwanted packages, the user is offered the ability to build a custom system by choosing among thousands of high-quality packages provided in the official repositories.

description.en: Three principles of Thumbtack's Thumbprint design system.
description.pl: Trzy zasady systemu designu Thumbprint Thumbtack.

principles.title: Build with a consistent process
principles.description: Use toolkits to identify, prioritise, and scope work. Build only what's essential after considering feedback, accessibility, and future use cases.

principles.title: Communicate and document everything
principles.description: Create a shared language for designers and developers. Respond quickly to questions, communicate changes, and refine documentation for reliable results.

principles.title: Encourage collaboration and feedback
principles.description: Encourage contributions and constructive criticism to establish trust. Spread system thinking to a diverse group to clarify what to build and what not to build.

description.en: Ten design principles from Weight Watchers (now WW).
description.pl: Dziesięć zasad designu Weight Watchers (obecnie WW).

principles.title: Personas
principles.description: Design for Weight Watchers members illustrated by product personas

principles.title: Experience
principles.description: Design for the entire product experience rather than isolated needs

principles.title: Context
principles.description: Keep context in mind – where's the member coming from and where are they going

principles.title: The 80%
principles.description: Optimize the design for the 80% use case - most members most of the time

principles.title: Simplicity
principles.description: Design for simplicity while supporting functionality, visual language and brand

principles.title: Patterns
principles.description: Design within the current product patterns when possible

principles.title: Extensibility
principles.description: Create new patterns when existing patterns don't solve a new problem. New patterns should be consistent and extensible.

principles.title: Platform
principles.description: Patterns should follow the native platform while still serving the brand

principles.title: Hierarchy
principles.description: Clearly define hierarchy and level of detail on each screen - focus on the main objective

principles.title: Empathy
principles.description: Design with member empathy

description.en: Seven design principles of the AMP web project.

principles.title: User Experience > Developer Experience > Ease of Implementation
principles.description: When in doubt, do what's best for the end user experience, even if it means that it's harder for the page creator to build or for the library developer to implement.

principles.title: Don't design for a hypothetical faster future browser
principles.description: We've chosen to build AMP as a library in the spirit of the EXTENSIBLE WEB MANIFESTO to be able to fix the web of today, not the web of tomorrow. AMP should be fast in today's browsers. When certain optimizations aren't possible with today's platform, AMP developers should participate in standards development to get these added to the web platform.

principles.title: Don't break the web
principles.description: Ensure that if AMP has outages or problems it doesn't hurt the rest of the web. That means if the Google AMP Cache, the URL API or the library fails it should be possible for websites and consumption apps to gracefully degrade. If something works with an AMP cache it should also work without a cache.

principles.title: Solve problems on the right layer
principles.description: E.g. don't integrate things on the client side, just because that is easier, when the user experience would be better with a server side integration.

principles.title: Only do things if they can be made fast
principles.description: Don't introduce components or features to AMP that can't reliably run at 60fps or hinder the instant load experience on today's most common mobile devices.

principles.title: Prioritise things that improve the user experience – but compromise when needed
principles.description: Some things can be made fast and are still a terrible user experience. AMPs should deliver a fantastic user experience and speed is just one part of that. Only compromise when lack of support for something would stop AMP from being widely used and deployed.

principles.title: No whitelists
principles.description: We won't give any special treatment to specific sites, domains or origins except where needed for security or performance reasons.

description.en: Ten principles of good road design from Highways England.
description.pl: Dziesięć zasad dobrego projektowania dróg z Highways England.

principles.title: makes roads safe and useful
principles.description: Safety is paramount. Roads must serve their purpose while protecting all users, including pedestrians and cyclists.

principles.title: is inclusive
principles.description: Design for everyone who uses the road, regardless of age, ability, or mode of transport.

principles.title: makes roads understandable
principles.description: Road layouts should be intuitive. Users should know what to do without confusion or excessive signage.

principles.title: fits in context
principles.description: Respect the landscape and local character. Roads should feel like they belong in their environment.

principles.title: is restrained
principles.description: Avoid overdesign. Use only what's necessary and resist adding elements that don't serve a clear purpose.

principles.title: is thorough
principles.description: Consider every detail and how elements work together. Quality comes from attention to the whole.

principles.title: is environmentally sustainable
principles.description: Minimise environmental impact during construction and operation. Support biodiversity and reduce carbon.

principles.title: is innovative
principles.description: Embrace new ideas and technologies that improve outcomes. Challenge established approaches when better solutions exist.

principles.title: is long-lasting
principles.description: Build for durability and future maintenance. Consider how the road will age and adapt over decades.

principles.title: is a collaborative process
principles.description: Involve communities, specialists, and stakeholders throughout. Good design emerges from diverse perspectives.

description.en: Six principles of OVO Energy's experience standard.
description.pl: Sześć zasad standardu doświadczenia OVO Energy.

principles.title: Intentional
principles.description: Focus on what matters using strategy, insights and data to inform decisions. Start by clearly defining the user problem or need, establish clear success criteria and metrics from the outset, and ensure every aspect of product and service has clear purpose and measurable impact.

principles.title: Inclusive
principles.description: Consider everyone by providing accessible, human and relatable designs. Be usable by everyone equally, create human connection when needed, and encourage positive behaviors. Ensure usability tests include diverse archetypes including those with accessibility needs.

principles.title: Connected
principles.description: Join the dots connecting offline and online to create seamless and coherent experiences. Be agnostic of organizational structures, design in the open, respond to user changes quickly, and maintain consistency throughout to avoid exposing internal fragmentation.

principles.title: Ethical
principles.description: Care about people and design with integrity to inspire trust and confidence. Build trust through transparency, present key decisions clearly and early, avoid deceptive patterns, and provide the right information at the right time with empathetic communication.

principles.title: Effortless
principles.description: Optimize for clarity by keeping things clear, simple and minimizing clutter. Always provide clear paths forward with no dead ends, ensure familiar interactions, and guide users to clear outcomes with clear next steps.

principles.title: Memorable
principles.description: Create compelling experiences by sweating every detail from pixels to letters. Craft with care and consideration, use bold and optimistic design language reflecting positive impact, and ensure quality is apparent in every touchpoint with harmony across all interactions.

description.en: Three principles of the Teamleader Ahoy design system.
description.pl: Trzy zasady systemu Ahoy od Teamleader.

principles.title: Simplicity
principles.description: Strip away the unnecessary and focus on what's essential. Clear navigation, minimalist interfaces, and intuitive interactions reduce cognitive load.

principles.title: Customisability
principles.description: Provide flexibility for users to personalise their experience through settings, themes, and layout options whilst maintaining design integrity.

principles.title: Free-Flowing
principles.description: Create seamless, fluid experiences with smooth animations and intuitive transitions. Each element feels in the right place, guiding users effortlessly.

description.en: Five principles for designing a clock that runs for 10,000 years.
description.pl: Pięć zasad projektowania zegara, który działa 10 000 lat.

principles.title: Longevity
principles.description: With occasional maintenance, the clock should reasonably be expected to display the correct time for the next 10,000 years.

principles.title: Maintainability
principles.description: The clock should be maintainable with bronze-age technology.

principles.title: Transparency
principles.description: It should be possible to determine operational principles of the clock by close inspection.

principles.title: Evolvability
principles.description: It should be possible to improve the clock with time.

principles.title: Scalability
principles.description: It should be possible to build working models of the clock from table-top to monumental size using the same design.

description.en: Four design principles from the consumer finance platform.

principles.title: Start with the story
principles.description: Since design decisions are geared toward solving a problem, always begin by understanding the objectives and intended outcomes of a project.

principles.title: Advocate for your audience
principles.description: Bringing clarity to the confusing industry of consumer finance means deeply understanding the mindset and motivations of our users in order to champion the best experiences for them.

principles.title: Consider every scenario
principles.description: Building a configurable platform to span millions of borrowers across hundreds of unique lenders requires a concise and flexible design language.

principles.title: Build a bridge to the future
principles.description: Reinventing an industry requires innovative approaches, but in order to drive adoption of new paradigms, both their function and value must be easily understood.

description.en: Three UX principles of the Michelin Design System.

principles.title: Low-environmental impact
principles.description: Work towards positive impact and light footprint through eco-design principles, conveying information simply and adding features for concrete needs with efficient optimisation.

principles.title: Inclusivity
principles.description: Aim for accessibility and usability for all users, creating simple and dependable interfaces through cultural sensitivity, regular testing, and WCAG standards.

principles.title: User-centric approach
principles.description: Focus first and foremost on user context to create coherent, stable and comfortable experiences, being transparent about data use and applying design thinking.

description.en: Three engineering team principles from Nava Public Benefit Corp.
description.pl: Trzy zasady inżynierskie zespołu Nava Public Benefit Corp.

principles.title: We are proactive
principles.description: Anticipate problems rather than react to them. Build systems that handle edge cases and find the simplest solution that works.

principles.title: We value the time of our colleagues, our users, and our future selves over our own
principles.description: Write code and documentation that saves others time. Consider the person who'll maintain this in two years.

principles.title: We believe in empathy, reliability, and simplicity
principles.description: Understand users' needs, build systems that work consistently, and avoid unnecessary complexity.

description.en: Nine design principles from Oxford Computer Consultants.

principles.title: Meet users early and often
principles.description: We meet user needs by meeting users regularly from the beginning of the project and throughout the process. The design and features we build are led by user feedback. Everyone in the team meets users, not only designers.

principles.title: Focus on adding value, not features
principles.description: Every feature or piece of functionality we add to the system should add value for users and the business. We should spend time and effort building the features that people need and want to use.

principles.title: Be commercially aware
principles.description: The whole team understands what is being commissioned: we get involved in the sales process and communicate our principles and practices to the customer throughout the project.

principles.title: Make it inclusive and accessible
principles.description: Inclusivity and accessibility are good for everyone. Everything we build should be accessible, inclusive and responsive by default.

principles.title: Test and iterate
principles.description: We are aware that our design solutions are assumptions until they are tested with real users. We experiment, test assumptions, learn and improve our ideas.

principles.title: Be consistent
principles.description: Being consistent helps with usability, efficiency and how users perceive the software (trust and professionalism).

principles.title: Make it attractive and usable
principles.description: Usable interface allows user to achieve their goals without friction. We also care about how our applications look and feel because attractive interfaces have an impact on perceived usability and users' trust.

principles.title: Be lean and efficient
principles.description: We spend our effort efficiently and remove any waste when communicating an idea, solving a problem or building the product.

principles.title: Collaborate
principles.description: We enjoy solving complex technical and design challenges – that's what we are best at. To really understand the problems and to solve them effectively, we work in small multidisciplinary teams.

description.en: Seven principles of the Sunrise Solar design system.

principles.title: Intuitive & Clear
principles.description: Use familiar patterns to make experiences easy to understand. Consider hierarchy, proximity, alignment, contrast, negative space and repetition.

principles.title: Considerate
principles.description: Base design decisions on industry standards, best practices and research data rather than opinions. Dive deep into the problem with clear purpose.

principles.title: Empowering
principles.description: Design components and interfaces to fully empower users to complete their tasks. Optimise for important tasks whilst giving access to more details if needed.

principles.title: Trustworthy
principles.description: Act as a trustworthy partner and treat users with respect. Be honest and transparent, eliminating unnecessary complexity and dark patterns.

principles.title: Adaptive
principles.description: Build experiences that work on every screen, platform and language. Components work seamlessly together in whichever combination suits user needs.

principles.title: Consistent
principles.description: Design for predictability. Consistent positions, styles and behaviours reduce mental load so users can focus on tasks rather than learning the UI.

principles.title: Accessible
principles.description: Design components to be accessible to everyone, inclusive towards people whose physical, mental or environmental conditions limit their performance.

description.en: Five principles of TPX Impact's design philosophy.
description.pl: Pięć zasad filozofii designu TPX Impact.

principles.title: People focused
principles.description: Put people at the centre of all work to create positive outcomes for citizens and organisations. Good design creates value by ensuring people outside the organisation can recognise the values that shape how the team works, making the impact of design visible and meaningful.

principles.title: Diverse reach and thinking
principles.description: Encourage diverse thinking through well-targeted user research and co-design work. Good design should work for everyone by bringing together different perspectives and approaches, ensuring solutions are inclusive and effective across diverse user groups and contexts.

principles.title: Visual and creative
principles.description: Create explorative, visual artefacts to support change and make work engaging. Good design should be creative and enjoyable, using visual approaches to make complex transformation programmes more accessible and to communicate ideas effectively.

principles.title: Ideas made real
principles.description: Learn by doing and prototyping to make design tangible and interactive. Good design is something people can directly interact with, allowing teams to test assumptions and iterate quickly through hands-on experimentation and making ideas concrete.

principles.title: Bold and ambitious
principles.description: Challenge the team and others to be bold and ambitious within constraints. Good design is about what can be made possible, pushing boundaries while working within the context of specific programmes, organisations, and stakeholder relationships to achieve transformative outcomes.

description.en: Three design principles from Basis.

principles.title: Build intentional and intuitive experiences
principles.description: Value user-friendly design over rigid consistency. Design with clear purpose and avoid unnecessary clutter.

principles.title: Serve diverse user needs
principles.description: Prioritise internal users while maintaining quality for external users. Anticipate needs and guide informed decisions.

principles.title: Design for users, not limitations
principles.description: Advocate for technology that amplifies user capabilities. Promote innovation and challenge the status quo.

description.en: Five principles of the Buildit Gravity design system.

principles.title: Inclusive
principles.description: Everything about Gravity, from the UI designs and components it provides to the way in which it is run and maintained should strive to be inclusive. That means removing barriers to entry for using or contributing to Gravity itself. That also means enabling products to be accessible to the broadest possible audience.

principles.title: Robust
principles.description: There is a lot we cannot control when it comes to digital products. Much of it we should not seek to control or restrict either. We can't decide what device, operating system, browser or settings people use when interacting with our products. Neither can we predict what the future might hold. And yet, the products we build need to embrace that uncertainty and handle all the diverse use-cases gracefully and reliably.

principles.title: Considered
principles.description: Everything about Gravity - be it design, tech or process - should exist for a reason. We should always be able to explain why something is the way it is. Wherever possible we should use data and research to drive our decisions. Failing that we should tap the experience and know-how of relevant experts.

principles.title: Lean
principles.description: Less is often more. Whether it's reducing waste while working on projects, writing terse code, designing focussed UIs or just avoiding fluffy language when communicating, leanness is something we value at Buildit. Gravity should therefore embody and support that as much as possible.

principles.title: Progressive
principles.description: Gravity is an opportunity for us to constantly try new things. New design directions. New technologies. New approaches towards designing and building user interfaces. We should take full advantage of this and strive to be a leader rather than a follower on all fronts.

description.en: Four principles of the Duet open source design system.
description.pl: Cztery zasady open source systemu Duet.

principles.title: Universality
principles.description: Universality is in the core of the World Wide Web, so we should embrace it and build systems that are available to, and accessible by, everyone.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: Consistency enhances clarity and makes our system more predictable and efficient to use. Users shouldn't have to wonder whether different actions or terminology used mean the same thing.

principles.title: Performance
principles.description: Good performance is good user experience. We should strive towards making our system as fast as possible in terms of both network footprint and the time it takes to become interactive.

principles.title: Modularity
principles.description: Modularity reduces complexity and improves our system's reusability by breaking it into small, easy to consume parts.

description.en: Three principles behind HTC Sense interface.

principles.title: Make It Mine
principles.description: Make It Mine is about feeling your HTC phone was created for and by you. To do this, HTC encourages you to dictate and organize how you want to access the people and content in your life in a way that fits best for you. For some, this means adding glance-view widgets that push content like twitter feeds, weather and other content to the surface while others may want quick access to business-focused information like email, calendar and world-times.

principles.title: Stay Close
principles.description: Today, staying in touch with the people in your life means managing a variety of communication channels and applications ranging from phone calls, emails, texts, photos, status updates and more. HTC Sense takes a different approach by integrating these communication channels and applications into one single view, enabling you to stay closer to your important people.

principles.title: Discover the Unexpected
principles.description: Many of the most memorable moments in your life are experienced, not explained. HTC Sense is focused on providing a variety of these simple yet innovative experiences on your HTC phone that will sometimes bring you moments of joy and delight. It can be something as basic as turning the phone over to silence a ring or as simple as improving the smart dialler for making calls quicker.

description.en: Five principles of the Kotti design system (acronym KOTTI).

principles.title: Keen
principles.description: The design should encourage users to be willing to engage with the product.

principles.title: Okay
principles.description: It's okay to not follow the foundation, but there should be a strong reason. It's okay to break the design principles but only when it's the only way to solve the requirement.

principles.title: Transparent
principles.description: By making design cues easy to perceive and detect, the user can process information smoothly without being aware of their presence.

principles.title: Timely
principles.description: The design needs to respond quickly and help the user finish their task in a timely matter.

principles.title: Intuitive
principles.description: The design should be intuitive and easy to understand, and decrease the learning curve.

description.en: Nine design tenets from National Instruments.

principles.title: Respect the History
principles.description: Change familiar patterns only when doing so is a clear improvement. Aim for migration, not just parity with previous versions.

principles.title: Stay Trustworthy
principles.description: NI users can process complex information. Build trust through accuracy and appropriate complexity—avoid oversimplification that causes frustration.

principles.title: Direct Focus
principles.description: Don't obscure the workspace. Elevate essential aspects and defer to the user's content, which should always be clear and readable.

principles.title: Be Cautious When Assuming User Intent
principles.description: Users need to feel in control. The frustration of fighting unwanted automation far exceeds the effort of doing a task manually.

principles.title: Promote Confidence
principles.description: Exploration depends on users predicting behaviour and trusting the experience is error-tolerant. Use consistent patterns and clear visual cues.

principles.title: Progressive Disclosure
principles.description: Reduce cognitive load by revealing complexity gradually. Help novices focus on priorities; save experts time scanning rarely-used features.

principles.title: Encourage Direct Manipulation
principles.description: Let users interact with objects directly for non-repeated tasks. It promotes rapid learning and makes actions easier to understand.

principles.title: Provide Batch Operations, and Promote Property Inheritance
principles.description: When objects are out of sight or actions span multiple items, provide a single place to apply settings rather than requiring direct manipulation.

principles.title: Provide the Appropriate Level of Scrappiness
principles.description: Allow non-linear workflows from multiple starting points, unless users might be overwhelmed or need guided, step-by-step progress.

description.en: Five design principles from TXI Digital.

principles.title: Humanity
principles.description: As advocates, pursue equitable and accessible design by addressing the needs of the most marginalized users, continuously testing with users and interrogating biases to create better experiences for everyone.

principles.title: Curiosity
principles.description: As researchers, pursue knowledge and understanding by questioning underlying purpose and impact, using evidence and data to guide discovery while interrogating assumptions and invalidating hypotheses.

principles.title: Ingenuity
principles.description: As innovators, respect existing tools and frameworks while borrowing inspiration from adjacent spaces, identifying connections between disparate ideas to combine elements in novel ways.

principles.title: Clarity
principles.description: As communicators, distill ideas to their essence through reframing and summarizing concepts, pushing for tangibility and specificity to pare things down for coherence and comprehension.

principles.title: Quality
principles.description: As craftspeople, create honest and aesthetic experiences through thoughtful experimentation and joyful exploration, balancing utility and beauty while ensuring everything is well made.

description.en: Ten principles from Codecademy's redesign.

principles.title: One Column
principles.description: Whenever possible, we have constrained our entire content to a single-column layout. This helped us focus on the core purpose of the page, while also giving us more control over our narrative. A one column layout was also easier to implement within our first responsive design system, by minimizing variation between different screens and form factors, such as mobile and tablet.

principles.title: Social Proof
principles.description: We never want to be arrogant, pretentious and dull in talking about ourselves, the features we have just launched, or how the product can change your life. In our new redesign we rely more frequently on our users and community to convey the benefits of Codecademy and the impact it had in their lives via quotes and testimonials.

principles.title: More Contrast
principles.description: Something you'll notice straight away in our new design is that we use color quite sparingly, and normally with a very defined purpose. For most part, color is associated with specific actions: hover states, primary and secondary buttons and controls. This way we can guarantee that our calls to action are very prominent and distinguishable from other surrounding elements.

principles.title: Fewer Form Fields
principles.description: All of us know how tiring, frustrating, and sometimes exasperating, it can be to fill long forms of personal information. Whenever we require input from our users we have tried to minimize the number questions and forms fields. Overall, this measure also tends to increase conversion rates and reduce users' typing fatigue.

principles.title: Keeping Focus
principles.description: We have always tried to reduce the number of calls to action in a single page, since we want users to focus on what matters the most, while also being able to single out the primary activity. One of our favorite design principles is Hick's Law, which says that time it takes for a user to make a decision depends on the number of choices available — the higher the number the longer the decision time.

principles.title: Direct Manipulation
principles.description: Whenever we have to decide between content (what users want to read, consume, and act upon) and chrome (actions, controls, and navigation), our answer is very swift: content should come first. As much as possible, we have allowed users to directly act upon UI elements for further contextual actions and controls, and in the process considerably minimize the amount of links and chrome on a page.

principles.title: Visual Hierarchy
principles.description: Visual hierarchy is critical to any graphic designer's work, and we have looked at it very closely when redesigning our 70+ pages. We have used typography, color and area to provide users with a clear content order that respects white space and recurrently gives their eyes a place to rest.

principles.title: Visual Recognition
principles.description: We all know that humans are much better at recognizing things they have previously seen or experienced, than recalling them from memory. This is why we have introduced throughout our ecosystem snapshots of users' in-progress projects.

principles.title: Larger Targets
principles.description: Another great universal design principle we love is Fitts's Law, which essentially says that the time required to move and interact with a target area is a function of the distance and size of the target. The closer and larger the target, the faster the action.

principles.title: Design for Edge Cases
principles.description: We know how intimidating and lonely an out of the box digital experience can be, where many features might still be disabled for newcomers. As part of our redesign, we wanted to optimize our first time user experience, to feel like a rich, welcoming place, where users feel confident in exploring further.

description.en: Five principles of designing with IBM Watson AI.
description.pl: Pięć zasad projektowania z IBM Watson AI.

principles.title: Know your data
principles.description: Become best friends with the dev and data scientists on the team. Engineers know the APIs like designers know grids. Build culture and trust. Keep teams lean and consistent. Put your confidence in them, and they will put theirs in you. Together you'll guide your team to narrow your focus on achievable realities based on your current data.

principles.title: Design for honesty, not omnipotence
principles.description: We need to know what Watson is telling our user — don't be confident and wrong. AI projects don't have normal bugs to solve. We have to design to solve for the user's expectations. If Watson's confidence is low, we need to make the user aware of that. We need to assume and design a fail state or a pivot point for to happen.

principles.title: Show — don't just do
principles.description: We have to open the door, let users peek into the black box of AI and let them know how Watson made that decision.
