Showing what Watson knows will help users feel confident in Watson's decisions but also allows them to course correct or improve Watson's knowledge at any time.

principles.title: Deliver insights, not visualizations
principles.description: Visualizations within the experience should address misconceptions, add to the end user outcome, and make the data easier to comprehend — visualizations are never the deliverable. The deliverable is an insight within it — but never a visualization alone.

principles.title: Always in service of people never in lieu of them
principles.description: The user and Watson are partners working towards mutual goals through an experience. We have to solve the user's need which is central to success but we also have to enable human and computer cooperation — not only interaction. Watson never makes a decision for a person — it finds, augment and educates.

description.en: Five UX principles of the VTS Terra design system.
description.pl: Pięć zasad UX systemu VTS Terra.

principles.title: Clear
principles.description: Ensure users are never confused by meeting them where they are in language and workflow. Prioritise accessibility and concise, focused information.

principles.title: Efficient
principles.description: Make working in VTS productive and performant. Pre-fill fields with sensible defaults, suggest actions, and hide infrequently-used functionality.

principles.title: Smart
principles.description: Enable users to do their jobs more effectively through trustworthy, actionable insights. Show how analytics were derived so users can share with confidence.

principles.title: Connected
principles.description: Products should feel part of the same ecosystem. Display information everywhere it's relevant and link related views so users don't need to hunt.

principles.title: Polished
principles.description: Ship thoughtful, crafted experiences. Use familiar patterns, deliver in vertical slices, and continuously evolve in response to user expectations.

description.en: Five principles of Dutch road safety doctrine.
description.pl: Pięć zasad holenderskiej doktryny bezpieczeństwa dróg.

principles.title: Functionality (of roads)
principles.description: Roads should have a clear function—either for through traffic or local access. Mixing functions creates confusion and danger.

principles.title: Homogeneity (of mass, speed and direction of road users)
principles.description: When different road users must share space, minimise differences in mass, speed, and direction to reduce crash severity.

principles.title: Predictability (of road course and road user behaviour)
principles.description: Road design should be so consistent that users instantly understand what to expect. The road itself communicates the rules.

principles.title: Forgivingness (of both the road/street environment and the road users)
principles.description: Humans make errors. Roads should be designed so mistakes don't automatically lead to crashes and injuries.

principles.title: State awareness (by the road user)
principles.description: Road users must be able to assess their own capabilities and the speeds of others. Design and education can support this.

description.en: Ten tenets of Chindogu — Japanese art of useless inventions.
description.pl: Dziesięć zasad Chindogu — japońska sztuka bezużytecznych wynalazków.

principles.title: A Chindogu cannot be for real use
principles.description: If you can actually use it without embarrassment, it's not a Chindogu. The invention must be almost but not quite practical.

principles.title: A Chindogu must exist
principles.description: You can't just imagine a Chindogu—it must be physically made. The act of creation is essential.

principles.title: Inherent in every Chindogu is the spirit of anarchy
principles.description: Chindogu challenge the assumption that everything must be useful. They question the relentless drive for efficiency.

principles.title: Chindogu are tools for everyday life
principles.description: They address real, mundane problems. The absurdity comes from the solution, not the problem itself.

principles.title: Chindogu are not for sale
principles.description: Commercialising a Chindogu defeats its purpose. They exist outside the market economy.

principles.title: Humour must not be the sole reason for creating Chindogu
principles.description: They may be funny, but they're not jokes. There must be a genuine attempt to solve a problem, however misguided.

principles.title: Chindogu are not propaganda
principles.description: They cannot carry political or social messages. Chindogu are innocent of ideology.

principles.title: Chindogu are never taboo
principles.description: They must be acceptable to everyone. Nothing offensive or inappropriate qualifies.

principles.title: Chindogu cannot be patented
principles.description: They belong to the world. Intellectual property claims contradict the spirit of Chindogu.

principles.title: Chindogu are without prejudice
principles.description: They must be usable by anyone regardless of age, gender, or background. No discrimination.

description.en: Six values and principles of the Atlassian Design System.
description.pl: Sześć wartości i zasad systemu Atlassian.

principles.title: Foundational (Value)
principles.description: Solve common problems for all to provide a solid foundation consumers can confidently build upon, avoiding consistency for its own sake whilst rejecting infinite flexibility.

principles.title: Trusted fundamentals before comprehensive patterns
principles.description: Focus on foundational problems first, providing opinionated building blocks that enable bespoke experiences whilst ensuring quality through research and clear accessibility, responsiveness, and reusability standards.

principles.title: Harmonious (Value)
principles.description: Create building blocks that work together to form a cohesive product family, gaining trust through intentional and purposeful design.

principles.title: Meeting system needs before delivering features
principles.description: Co-create with all perspectives, finish what you start before beginning new work, incorporate continuous feedback, and consider documentation, support, deprecation, and maintenance from the outset.

principles.title: Empowering, for everyone (Value)
principles.description: Make the design system accessible to everyone regardless of discipline, skill level, or tenure, multiplying impact by enabling as many people as possible to use it.

principles.title: Bringing people on the journey before helping for the moment
principles.description: Educate consumers through the process to build trust and shared ownership, prioritise service experience, optimise for self-service, and inspire consumers to become champions who improve their craft.

description.en: Seventeen iOS User Experience Guidelines from Apple.
description.pl: Siedemnaście zasad UX iOS od Apple.

principles.title: Focus on the Primary Task
principles.description: When an iOS app establishes and maintains focus on its primary task, it is satisfying and enjoyable to use. To maintain that focus, you need to determine what's most important in each context or screen. Analyze what's needed in each screen. As you decide what to display, always ask yourself: Is this critical information or functionality users need right now?

principles.title: Elevate the Content that People Care About
principles.description: In a game, people care about the experience; they don't expect to manage, consume, or create content. If you're developing a game, you elevate content by enhancing the experience with a satisfying story, beautiful graphics, and responsive gameplay.

principles.title: Think Top Down
principles.description: The top of the screen is most visible to people, because they tend to interact with the device by holding the device in the following ways: In their nondominant hand—or laying it on a surface—and gesturing with a finger of the dominant hand.

principles.title: Give People a Logical Path to Follow
principles.description: People appreciate knowing where they are in an app and getting confirmation that they're on the right path. Make the path through the information you present logical and easy for users to predict.

principles.title: Make Usage Easy and Obvious
principles.description: Strive to make your app instantly understandable to people, because you can't assume that they have the time—or can spare the attention—to figure out how it works.

principles.title: Use User-Centric Terminology
principles.description: In all your text-based communication with users, use terminology you're sure they understand. Use what you know about your users to determine whether the words and phrases you plan to use are appropriate.

principles.title: Minimize the Effort Required for User Input
principles.description: Inputting information takes time and attention, whether people tap controls or use the keyboard. If your app requires a lot of user input before anything useful happens, that input slows people down and can discourage them from using your app.

principles.title: Downplay File-Handling Operations
principles.description: Although iOS apps can allow people to create and manipulate files, this does not mean that people should have an awareness of a file system on an iOS device.

principles.title: Enable Collaboration and Connectedness
principles.description: iOS devices are personal devices, but they also encourage collaboration and sharing with others. Enhance your app by helping people collaborate and connect with others.

principles.title: De-emphasize Settings
principles.description: Avoid including settings in your app if you can. Settings include preferred app behaviors and information that people rarely want to change. Users can't open the Settings app without first switching away from your app.

principles.title: Brand Appropriately
principles.description: Incorporate a brand's colors or images in a refined, unobtrusive way. Branding is most effective when it's subtle and understated.

principles.title: Make Search Quick and Rewarding
principles.description: In apps that handle or display a lot of data, search can be a primary function. If you need to provide search in your app, follow these guidelines to ensure that it performs well.

principles.title: Entice and Inform with a Well-Written Description
principles.description: Your App Store description is a great opportunity to communicate with potential users. In addition to describing your app accurately and highlighting the qualities you think people might appreciate the most.

principles.title: Be Succinct
principles.description: Think like a newspaper editor, and strive to convey information in a condensed, headline style. When your UI text is short and direct, users can absorb it quickly and easily.

principles.title: Use UI Elements Consistently
principles.description: People expect standard views and controls to look and behave consistently across apps. Follow the recommended usages for standard user interface elements.

principles.title: Consider Adding Physicality and Realism
principles.description: When appropriate, add a realistic, physical dimension to your app. Sometimes, the more true to life your app looks and behaves, the easier it is for people to understand how it works and the more they enjoy using it.

principles.title: Delight People with Stunning Graphics
principles.description: Rich, beautiful, engaging graphics draw people into an app and make the simplest task rewarding. Beautiful artwork also helps to build your app's brand in people's eyes.

description.en: Five design principles for Android Wear OS smartwatches.
description.pl: Pięć zasad designu Android Wear OS dla smartwatchy.

principles.title: Design for critical tasks
principles.description: Focus on one or two tasks rather than a full app experience, prioritising essential functionality that users need to accomplish quickly on their wrist.

principles.title: Optimize for the wrist
principles.description: Help people complete tasks on the watch within seconds to avoid ergonomic discomfort or arm fatigue, designing for quick interactions that respect wearable form factors.

principles.title: Better together
principles.description: Consider which actions are appropriate for each device, using watches for quick frequent tasks while mobile devices handle prolonged and complex interactions.

principles.title: Always relevant
principles.description: Keep content on the watch face relevant to the user by updating app content based on their context such as time, place and current activity.

principles.title: Works offline
principles.description: Design for slow connections and offline use cases such as exercising and commuting, ensuring functionality remains available without constant connectivity.

description.en: Four principles for crafting elegant business tools at Facebook.
description.pl: Cztery zasady projektowania eleganckich narzędzi biznesowych Facebook.

principles.title: Help people learn and grow
principles.description: Teach people to make the best choices through personalized guidance, increasing their confidence and success by designing experiences that help them constantly become more effective at their jobs.

principles.title: Balance efficiency and effectiveness
principles.description: Improve how people work so they achieve objectives with minimal effort, streamlining tasks while ensuring the right outcomes by focusing on business goals rather than just speed.

principles.title: Bring clarity to complexity
principles.description: Create intuitive ways for people to tackle complicated topics and workflows by finding the optimal balance between simplification and access to advanced functionality for different expertise levels.

principles.title: Be accurate and predictable
principles.description: Provide reliable controls and relevant feedback that build trust in products, ensuring business applications perform consistently to prevent financial loss and customer issues.

description.en: Five principles of the BBC's Global Experience Language.
description.pl: Pięć zasad BBC Global Experience Language.

principles.title: Respect everyone
principles.description: Create a personalised experience for every individual - whatever their needs, schedule and interests.

principles.title: Love needs
principles.description: Design to the needs of your audience. Every innovation has to benefit or delight them.

principles.title: Everywhere, always
principles.description: Consider every screen and where, when and why it might be used - from the armchair to the Arctic.

principles.title: Drive discovery
principles.description: The journey's as important as the destination. And if your user veers off in a new, exciting direction along the way, all the better.

principles.title: Further together
principles.description: Upcycle existing designs. It'll give you more time to innovate. And the greater consistency will encourage greater exploration of the BBC, Online.

description.en: Eight Windows User Experience Design Principles.

principles.title: Reduce concepts to increase confidence
principles.description: Have you introduced a new concept? Why? Is it necessary? Can you get rid of unneeded concepts? Are you making meaningful distinctions? Does the UX continue the same concept?

principles.title: Small things matter, good and bad
principles.description: What are the important 'small things' seen often or by many? What small problems are you solving? Do less better. Don't cut the small things in your experiences. Plan for the thoughtful details. Fix the small bugs.

principles.title: Be great at look and do
principles.description: What is your UX great at? Does its look reflect what it is great at? Does the first thing users see reflect what the UX is great at? Does the UX match expectations? Is it obvious what users can do? Are you providing only the necessary steps?

principles.title: Solve distractions, not discoverability
principles.description: Reduce distractions. Don't let features compete with themselves. Commit to new functionality.

principles.title: UX before knobs and questions
principles.description: Turn down the volume of questions. Ask once. Don't require configuration to get value. Was the question asked already? Look for opportunities to consolidate.

principles.title: Personalization, not customization
principles.description: Does the feature allow users to express an element of themselves? Have you made the distinction between personalization and customization?

principles.title: Value the life cycle of the experience
principles.description: Consider the user experience at all stages: Installation and creation. First use and customization. Regular use. Management and maintenance. Uninstall or upgrade.

principles.title: Time matters, so build for people on the go
principles.description: All UX principles apply equally at 12-inch and 20-inch screen sizes. Be interruptible. Account for starting and stopping. Account for getting and losing connectivity. Performance is the universal UX killer.

description.en: Fourteen standards that all UK government digital services must meet.
description.pl: Czternaście standardów które muszą spełniać cyfrowe usługi rządu UK.

principles.title: Understand users and their needs
principles.description: Take time to understand who uses the service and what they need. Base decisions on research, not assumptions.

principles.title: Solve a whole problem for users
principles.description: Work to address the complete user journey, not just the part your organisation is responsible for.

principles.title: Provide a joined up experience across all channels
principles.description: Ensure the service works well whether users access it online, by phone, or in person.

principles.title: Make the service simple to use
principles.description: Build something that's easy to understand and navigate. If it's too complicated, people won't use it.

principles.title: Make sure everyone can use the service
principles.description: Design for people with different needs and abilities. The service must be accessible to all who need it.

principles.title: Have a multidisciplinary team
principles.description: Bring together people with different skills and perspectives. Good services need diverse expertise.

principles.title: Use agile ways of working
principles.description: Work in short cycles, respond to change, and deliver value incrementally rather than all at once.

principles.title: Iterate and improve frequently
principles.description: Keep improving the service based on what you learn. Launch early and refine based on real feedback.

principles.title: Create a secure service which protects users' privacy
principles.description: Evaluate security and privacy risks and address them appropriately. Collect only the data you need.

principles.title: Define what success looks like and publish performance data
principles.description: Set clear metrics for success and share how the service is performing publicly.

principles.title: Choose the right tools and technology
principles.description: Select technology that fits the problem and can be maintained long-term. Avoid unnecessary complexity.

principles.title: Make new source code open
principles.description: Publish code openly by default. This improves transparency and allows others to learn from your work.

principles.title: Use and contribute to open standards, common components and patterns
principles.description: Build on existing solutions where they exist. Share what you create so others can benefit.

principles.title: Operate a reliable service
principles.description: Minimise downtime and have plans for when things go wrong. Users depend on the service being available.

description.en: Five People Principles guiding Audible employees.

principles.title: Be Customer Obsessed
principles.description: Anchor every decision in deep understanding of and dedication to the listener's experience.

principles.title: Imagine and Invent Before They Ask
principles.description: Anticipate user needs rather than react — invent before customers can articulate the gap.

principles.title: Articulate the Possible and Move Fast to Make it Real
principles.description: Translate vision into tangible work quickly, prototyping the future rather than just describing it.

principles.title: Study and Draw Inspiration from Culture and Technology
principles.description: Stay curious about trends in culture and tech to inform original product thinking.

principles.title: Activate Caring
principles.description: Express genuine care for colleagues and customers through actions, not just intent.

description.en: Five C principles from Australia's DesignGov initiative.

principles.title: Connected, Customer and Community Centric
principles.description: Build services that connect across agencies while centering on citizens and community needs.

principles.title: Courageous
principles.description: Be willing to take bold approaches and challenge conventional government delivery.

principles.title: Collaborative, Co-design, Co-creation, Co-production
principles.description: Involve citizens, public servants, and stakeholders as partners in designing services together.

principles.title: Coherent
principles.description: Provide one consistent voice and experience across government touchpoints.

principles.title: Co-sponsored
principles.description: Share ownership and accountability for design across departments and levels of government.

description.en: Ten Bing design principles documented by Luke Wroblewski.
description.pl: Dziesięć zasad designu Bing udokumentowanych przez Luke'a Wroblewskiego.

principles.title: Design for explorers
principles.description: Target the 25% of searchers who are willing to try new technology, enjoy surprises, and dig deeper into results.

principles.title: Delight and surprise our users
principles.description: Create engaging experiences that go beyond basic functionality.

principles.title: Earn Trust
principles.description: Build credibility through consistent, reliable performance and design choices.

principles.title: Be the brand
principles.description: Establish a distinctive identity that represents Microsoft's search offering.

principles.title: Make money
principles.description: A specific color of blue drove $80-$100 million dollars a year — design decisions have revenue impact.

principles.title: Showcase our best
principles.description: Present the strongest content and features prominently.

principles.title: Organize the page by relevance
principles.description: Structure information so users can find what matters most efficiently.

principles.title: Respect the need for speed
principles.description: User engagement dropped significantly even with only a 1 second delay.

description.en: Ten Core Values that famously define the Zappos culture.

principles.title: Deliver WOW Through Service
principles.description: Go beyond what's expected — exceptional service should genuinely surprise customers.

principles.title: Embrace and Drive Change

principles.title: Create Fun and A Little Weirdness
principles.description: Inject personality and play into everyday work — quirky is part of the brand.

principles.title: Be Adventurous, Creative, and Open-Minded
principles.description: Stay curious, try new approaches, and welcome perspectives different from your own.

principles.title: Pursue Growth and Learning
principles.description: Treat your role as a vehicle for personal and professional development.

principles.title: Build Open and Honest Relationships With Communication
principles.description: Trust grows from frank, direct, and respectful conversation — not avoidance.

principles.title: Build a Positive Team and Family Spirit
principles.description: Treat colleagues as family; positivity is a team responsibility.

principles.title: Do More With Less
principles.description: Resourcefulness over abundance — constraints sharpen creativity.

principles.title: Be Passionate and Determined
principles.description: Care deeply about what you build; persistence outlasts talent.

principles.title: Be Humble
principles.description: Stay grounded — pride should never block learning or collaboration.

description.en: Ten Usability Heuristics — UX foundational classic.

principles.title: Visibility of system status
principles.description: The system should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within reasonable time.

principles.title: Match between system and the real world
principles.description: The system should speak the users' language, with words, phrases and concepts familiar to the user, rather than system-oriented terms. Follow real-world conventions, making information appear in a natural and logical order.

principles.title: User control and freedom
principles.description: Users often choose system functions by mistake and will need a clearly marked 'emergency exit' to leave the unwanted state without having to go through an extended dialogue. Support undo and redo.

principles.title: Consistency and standards
principles.description: Users should not have to wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing. Follow platform conventions.

principles.title: Error prevention
principles.description: Even better than good error messages is a careful design which prevents a problem from occurring in the first place. Either eliminate error-prone conditions or check for them and present users with a confirmation option before they commit to the action.

principles.title: Recognition rather than recall
principles.description: Minimize the user's memory load by making objects, actions, and options visible. The user should not have to remember information from one part of the dialogue to another. Instructions for use of the system should be visible or easily retrievable whenever appropriate.

principles.title: Flexibility and efficiency of use
principles.description: Accelerators — unseen by the novice user — may often speed up the interaction for the expert user such that the system can cater to both inexperienced and experienced users. Allow users to tailor frequent actions.

principles.title: Aesthetic and minimalist design
principles.description: Dialogues should not contain information which is irrelevant or rarely needed. Every extra unit of information in a dialogue competes with the relevant units of information and diminishes their relative visibility.

principles.title: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
principles.description: Error messages should be expressed in plain language (no codes), precisely indicate the problem, and constructively suggest a solution.

principles.title: Help and documentation
principles.description: Even though it is better if the system can be used without documentation, it may be necessary to provide help and documentation. Any such information should be easy to search, focused on the user's task, list concrete steps to be carried out, and not be too large.

description.en: SOLID — five OOP design principles by Robert C. Martin.
description.pl: SOLID — pięć zasad OOP Roberta C. Martina.

principles.title: Single Responsibility Principle
principles.description: A class should only have a single responsibility, that is, only changes to one part of the software's specification should be able to affect the specification of the class.

principles.title: Open Closed Principle
principles.description: Software entities should be open for extension, but closed for modification.

principles.title: Liskov Substitution Principle
principles.description: Objects in a program should be replaceable with instances of their subtypes without altering the correctness of that program.

principles.title: Interface Segregation Principle
principles.description: Many client-specific interfaces are better than one general-purpose interface.

principles.title: Dependency Inversion Principle
principles.description: One should depend upon abstractions, rather than concrete implementations.

description.en: Five meta-principles for writing design principles.

principles.title: Be purposeful
principles.description: Define how and why design principles will be used before creating them. Consider what decisions they need to influence and what 'good' looks like for your specific context.

principles.title: Be yourself
principles.description: Ground principles in your own organisation's knowledge, users, and business context rather than copying others. Avoid reviewing competitors' principles to maintain originality.

principles.title: Be actionable
principles.description: Focus on how the experience should feel rather than outcomes. Ensure principles can guide concrete decisions and identify examples that do and don't demonstrate each principle.

principles.title: Be considered
principles.description: Iterate and test principles with careful attention to language. Allow time for refinement and consider different ways of articulating each principle's message.

principles.title: Be maintained
principles.description: Establish an owner responsible for making decisions, communicating value, and keeping principles as a living reference that teams actually use in practice.

description.en: Thirteen plays for delivering digital services in US government.
description.pl: Trzynaście praktyk dostarczania usług cyfrowych w rządzie USA.

principles.title: Understand what people need
principles.description: Begin by exploring the needs of real users. Let people's needs—not government structures—inform technical and design decisions.

principles.title: Address the whole experience, from start to finish
principles.description: Understand all the ways people interact with the service, online and offline. Every encounter should move users closer to their goal.

principles.title: Make it simple and intuitive
principles.description: Using a government service shouldn't be stressful or confusing. Build services simple enough that users succeed the first time, unaided.

principles.title: Build the service using agile and iterative practices
principles.description: Use incremental development to reduce risk. Get working software into users' hands early and adjust based on feedback.

principles.title: Structure budgets and contracts to support delivery
principles.description: Work with experienced budgeting officers. Contracts should allow for prototyping, frequent milestones, and flexibility.

principles.title: Assign one leader and hold that person accountable
principles.description: A single product owner must have authority to make decisions and be accountable for whether the service meets user needs.

principles.title: Bring in experienced teams
principles.description: Assemble teams with proven experience building digital services. Include designers, developers, and product managers who've done this before.

principles.title: Choose a modern technology stack
principles.description: Select flexible, commonly-used technologies that allow the team to work efficiently and adapt as needs change.

principles.title: Deploy in a flexible hosting environment
principles.description: Use infrastructure that can scale with demand and allows rapid deployment of changes without lengthy procurement.

principles.title: Automate testing and deployments
principles.description: Build automated tests and deployment pipelines so new features can be added frequently and released with confidence.

principles.title: Manage security and privacy through reusable processes
principles.description: Integrate security and privacy from the start using repeatable processes rather than treating them as afterthoughts.

principles.title: Use data to drive decisions
principles.description: Collect and analyse data on how the service is performing. Let evidence guide improvements rather than assumptions.

principles.title: Default to open
principles.description: Work in the open, publish code openly, and use open standards. Transparency improves quality and builds trust.

description.en: Seven principles for knowing when to stop designing.
description.pl: Siedem zasad wiedzy kiedy przestać projektować.

principles.title: Stop when the next change is for you, not the user
principles.description: If the improvement satisfies taste or the need for creativity rather than solving a problem, it's no longer meaningful.

principles.title: Stop when the problem isn't proven
principles.description: If you can't point to evidence, you're making an assumption.

principles.title: Stop when the question shifts from why to how
principles.description: Once the focus shifts to execution, the design decision has already been made.

principles.title: Stop when you're redesigning not refining
principles.description: If each iteration opens new questions rather than closes them, you've started over without admitting it.

principles.title: Stop when the design can't be tested in its current form
principles.description: If it can't be put in front of users, it's not ready for more work.

principles.title: Stop when you're designing for edge cases
principles.description: When rare scenarios start driving decisions, the centre hasn't been resolved yet.

principles.title: Stop to allow time to learn
principles.description: The gap between designing and releasing is where you find out if you were right.

description.en: Seven principles for 21st century government.

principles.title: Design for people's needs
principles.description: Center service design around real citizen needs, not bureaucratic structures.

principles.title: Make it easy for everyone to participate
principles.description: Lower barriers to participation in democratic and civic processes.

principles.title: Focus on what government can do
principles.description: Be honest about government's role — neither overpromise nor abdicate responsibility.

principles.title: Make data easy to find and use
principles.description: Treat government data as public infrastructure — open, machine-readable, well-documented.

principles.title: Use data to make and improve decisions
principles.description: Let evidence inform policy and service delivery, not just intuition.

principles.title: Choose the right technology for the job
principles.description: Match tech to need; resist legacy procurement and shiny-object syndrome.

principles.title: Organize for results
principles.description: Structure teams and processes around outcomes for citizens, not internal hierarchy.

description.en: Six principles for designing across multiple devices.
description.pl: Sześć zasad projektowania na wielu urządzeniach.

principles.title: Recognize Interdependence
principles.description: Devices don't exist in isolation. Design for how they work together, not just how each works alone.

principles.title: Embrace Diversity
principles.description: Different devices serve different purposes. Celebrate their unique strengths rather than forcing uniformity.

principles.title: Support Exchanges
principles.description: Enable smooth handoffs between devices. Users should move fluidly from phone to tablet to desktop.

principles.title: Ensure Resiliency
principles.description: Systems should degrade gracefully. When one device or connection fails, the experience should continue.

principles.title: Integrate Naturally
principles.description: Multi-device interactions should feel effortless. Don't make users think about the technology.

principles.title: Expect Evolution
principles.description: New devices will emerge and old ones will change. Design systems that can adapt over time.

description.en: Sixteen first principles of interaction design — Tog's classic.
description.pl: Szesnaście podstawowych zasad interaction designu — klasyk Toga.

principles.title: Anticipation
principles.description: Bring users all the information and tools they need for each step. Predict what they'll want next rather than making them search for it.

principles.title: Autonomy
principles.description: Give users control over their environment while maintaining sensible boundaries. People feel most comfortable when they can explore without hazard.

principles.title: Color Blindness
principles.description: Never use colour as the only means of conveying information. Roughly 10% of men have some form of colour blindness.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: Maintain consistency at multiple levels—platform, application, and within features. But break consistency deliberately when it aids understanding.

principles.title: Defaults
principles.description: Choose intelligent defaults that serve most users. Make them easy to change and use clear language to explain what restoration options actually do.

principles.title: Efficiency of the User
principles.description: Optimise for human productivity, not machine efficiency. People cost far more than computers, so save their time first.

principles.title: Explorable Interfaces
principles.description: Let users move freely backward and forward through workflows. Clear, visible navigation encourages people to complete tasks.

principles.title: Fitts' Law
principles.description: Target acquisition time depends on distance and size. Make important controls large and position them near screen edges where the cursor stops naturally.

principles.title: Human Interface Objects
principles.description: Create objects that behave consistently and can be manipulated directly. Users should be able to predict how objects will respond.

principles.title: Latency Reduction
principles.description: Reduce actual wait times and make unavoidable delays feel shorter. Acknowledge input immediately and show progress indicators.

principles.title: Learnability
principles.description: Balance learnability with usability for experienced users. The ideal interface works well for both novices and experts.

principles.title: Metaphors
principles.description: Use metaphors that help users understand new concepts through familiar ones. But don't let the metaphor limit what the software can do.

principles.title: Protect Users' Work
principles.description: Ensure users never lose their work through system failure, their own error, or misunderstanding. Save continuously and enable recovery.

principles.title: Readability
principles.description: Text must be readable. Use high contrast, appropriate sizes, and avoid visual tricks that sacrifice legibility for style.

principles.title: Track State
principles.description: Remember where users are and what they've done. Restore their context when they return rather than forcing them to start over.

principles.title: Visible Navigation
principles.description: Make navigation visible and predictable. Users should always know where they are, where they can go, and how to get back.

description.en: Seven principles for conversational interfaces from Google.
description.pl: Siedem zasad interfejsów konwersacyjnych od Google.

principles.title: Keep it short
principles.description: Respect users' time. Get to the point and get out of the way.

principles.title: Give them credit
principles.description: People know the language and they know how to talk, so avoid telling them how to speak and putting words in their mouth. Instead focus on natural ways to progress the dialog forward.

principles.title: Optimize for relevance
principles.description: Be contextually relevant and sensitive to the user's current need and the environment a user might be in.

principles.title: Delight the ear without distracting the mind
principles.description: When adding personality, be sure it's not so over the top as to interfere with a user's task.

principles.title: Engage beginners and attract experts
principles.description: Designing for many people doesn't mean designing for the lowest common denominator.

principles.title: Take turns
principles.description: Don't take back your turn prematurely. If you ask the user a question (yield your turn), don't throw in an additional instruction that gets in the way of their right to answer you.

principles.title: Don't read minds
principles.description: Give them the facts and let them decide.
